Michal Faferek
data.message:
gateway/opcua: only external components own bare-id faults

Restore the #516 guardrail broken by the PLC_COMMS_LOST scope fix: an
internal component must not claim faults reported under its bare id.
The real gap was the opcua plugin never marking its component external;
fix that instead of widening the scope grant to every component.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
gateway/opcua: advertised capabilities must match served resources

DataProvider/OperationProvider gain has_data/has_operations (default
true); PluginManager stops routing entities the provider cannot serve,
so capabilities stay honest. opcua: grouping component and the alarms
fallback app no longer advertise data/operations/x-plc-data they 404.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fault_manager: count occurrences on edges, not per report

occurrence_count no longer increments on every FAILED re-report of an
active fault - only on first raise and reactivation after CLEARED.
Reactivation also resets first_occurred to the new cycle.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
gateway: advertise only served capabilities for plugin entities

Plugin-owned entities advertised data/operations hrefs that 404 by
contract when the plugin registers no Data/OperationProvider - dead
links every SOVD client follows. Prune them from the detail
capability lists.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fault_manager: record confirmed_at_ns in the sqlite store

Stamp the transition into CONFIRMED (report, reactivation and
time-based paths) into a new confirmed_at_ns column; older DBs are
migrated with 0 = unknown. Consumed by the compliance timeline,
whose records carried confirmed_at_ns null.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
opcua: pass occurrence data through entity-scoped fault lists

list_faults dropped first/last_occurred, occurrence_count and
severity_label and always served an empty source_id, so clients
rendered 'time unknown'. Pass the fields through and derive
source_id from reporting_sources.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
gateway: treat components as fault reporting sources in scope resolution

Component-scoped fault queries collected only child-app FQNs, so
faults reported under the component's own id (PLC_COMMS_LOST from
bridge plugins) returned empty on /components/<id>/faults while the
instance route listed them. Always include the component id.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
gateway: reject fault-trigger rules on nonexistent data points

POST /fault-triggers accepted any data_name and listed the rule as
active even when the app has no such point - a silently dead alarm.
Validate against the app's discovered points (400 lists the valid
names); unenumerable points (PLC offline) still skip the check.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
gateway: config-less fault-trigger threshold engine at /fault-triggers

Runtime threshold rules on discovered data points: cross fires a SOVD fault,
un-cross auto-clears; rules persist to JSON and are edited over REST at
/api/v1/apps/{app_id}/fault-triggers. Kept as a sibling of /triggers, which
stays the SOVD notification-trigger CRUD - the two share no schema or store.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
opcua: infer writable from server AccessLevel, width-typed integer writes

auto_browse now reads each Variable's AccessLevel/UserAccessLevel and marks
the point writable when the session's CurrentWrite bit is set (new
auto_browse.infer_writable flag, default on; explicit node_map still wins).
Integer writes probe the node's real DataType and write the matching scalar
width, so narrow types like the S7 Int (Int16) no longer get BadTypeMismatch.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
opcua: clang-format fixes in network_discovery

Two lines in network_discovery.{hpp,cpp} failed clang-format-18
against the repo config. Formatting only, no behaviour change.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
opcua: config-less component identity + native A&C faults, ODR/visibility hardening

Zero-config discovery now names the SOVD component from the device's own
read identity (DI nameplate manufacturer+model, else BuildInfo
ProductName, else opcua-<host>) instead of a hardcoded "OpenPLC Runtime"
default, and auto-enables native Alarms & Conditions (Server EventNotifier
i=2253) when no node map and no explicit auto_alarms block are given, so
discovered conditions surface on /api/v1/faults with a derived fault_code.

Rename the plugin's DiscoveryConfig to OpcuaDiscoveryConfig and build the
.so with -fvisibility=hidden -fvisibility-inlines-hidden so its internals
cannot interpose another plugin's symbols when the gateway dlopens all
plugins into one process (the extern "C" entry points stay exported).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test: harden integration-test launches under coverage and fix timing races

Under a coverage (gcov) build a gateway or fault manager must flush coverage
data at shutdown, which can exceed the launch default SIGTERM window (~10s)
and get the process SIGKILLed to -9, failing the post-shutdown exit-code
check. Only create_gateway_node set a wide enough window; tests that built
the node inline (test_scripts_api, test_updates, test_update_status_subscription,
test_triggers_persistent, test_tls) missed it, and create_fault_manager_node
had no window at all - a latent risk for the many tests that launch a fault
manager through create_test_launch.

Extend create_gateway_node with name= and extra_env=, give
create_fault_manager_node the same name=/extra_env= plus the shutdown windows,
then route the inline gateways and fault managers through the two helpers. This
fixes the SIGKILL failure, restores the coverage env the aggregation peers and
fault managers had dropped, and removes four hand-copied shutdown-window
constants. test_tls keeps its inline gateway (params file) but gets the windows
directly and a post-shutdown exit-code check it was missing. The two
subprocess.Popen demo spawns now also carry the coverage env.

Route each subprocess's coverage to its own package: create_fault_manager_node
and create_demo_nodes passed the default gateway package to get_coverage_env,
so their .gcda were written into the gateway build dir (lost for their own
package, noise for the gateway). Pass ros2_medkit_fault_manager and
ros2_medkit_integration_tests respectively.

The fault-manager-side tests build the node inline in their own packages (they
cannot import create_fault_manager_node, which lives downstream), so give the
inline fault_manager_node the same windows directly in test_rosbag_integration,
test_integration, test_rosbag_entity_scope, test_entity_thresholds_integration
(fault_manager) and the diagnostic_bridge, log_bridge and action_status_bridge
integration tests.

Extend the windows to every other coverage-instrumented C++ node that a
post-shutdown exit-code check guards, not just the fault_manager beside it:
the three bridge nodes that are the actual subject under test
(diagnostic_bridge_node, log_bridge_node, action_status_bridge_node), the demo
nodes launched through create_demo_nodes, and the inline demo-node launches in
the discovery, graph-provider and beacon feature tests. Each is a small binary,
but the exit-code checks reject -9 and only create_gateway_node /
create_fault_manager_node carried the window, so a slow-runner gcov flush past
the default SIGTERM window would SIGKILL them to -9 the same way.

Fix the timing/isolation inconsistencies found while tracing this:
- Poll GetRosbag and GetSnapshots until the async capture is written instead
  of a fixed sleep plus a single call, and poll for the rosbag buffer publisher
  and the cleanup delete. The snapshot test relies on _wait_for_snapshot (which
  polls GetSnapshots for the real capture) as its gate rather than a pre-wait on
  the short-lived on-demand subscription.
- Prime the ring buffer before the multi-fault rosbag test confirms its first
  fault: a prior fault's post-fault recording window keeps new messages out of
  the buffer, so it could be empty at confirmation and flush_to_bag created no
  bag. Subscribe to the recorded topic (matching its BEST_EFFORT QoS) and wait
  for fresh messages before reporting the fault.
- Republish the ERROR log in the log_bridge test until the fault appears: a
  single publish raced the bridge's report client discovering the fault manager
  (the second discovery hop), which the /rosout subscription wait does not cover.
- Gate the update SSE test on the reader thread opening the stream (a
  threading.Event) rather than a fixed sleep.
- test_opcua_secured hardcoded ROS_DOMAIN_ID=228, which collides with the
  domain CMake assigns test_opcua_identity; move it to the free 229.

Fix a ThreadSanitizer data race in test_ros2_parameter_transport: TearDown
called executor->cancel() while the spin thread was still inside spin_some(),
racing the executor's notify-waitable (ExecutorNotifyWaitable::is_ready vs
trigger_entity_recollect). Clear the run flag and join the spin thread before
touching the executor; the spin_some(10ms) loop exits on its own, so cancel()
is not needed.

Give the sanitizer jobs timeout headroom so a slow runner does not cancel them
mid-run: a full ASan run is ~55 min (bump 60 -> 90) and a full TSan run is
~40 min (bump 45 -> 60). Both were cancelling intermittently at the old limits.

Closes #553

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): fold node reachability into pipeline_status

pipeline_status was rolled up from edges only, so a Function with a dead
scoped node read as "healthy": an offline app carries no topics, produces no
edge, and the surviving edges stay active. Fold node reachability in - any
unreachable scoped node now makes pipeline_status at least "degraded" (a
stale edge still outranks it as "broken"), and node_status names which node.

Also correct the multi_publisher kSuppress comment and docs. Suppressing an
ambiguous rate removes the misleading number, not the health verdict, so it
does not by itself stop a broken pipeline from reading healthy - rate_ambiguous
already flags the ambiguity.

Add unit tests (build and HTTP-handler paths) and an end-to-end launch test
that kills a manifest-scoped node and asserts the served graph goes from
healthy to degraded with that node unreachable.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration): expect engine-temp-monitor app in hybrid suppression test

The demo manifest defines the engine-temp-monitor App (the graph-provider
consumer that subscribes to /powertrain/engine/temperature, giving the
demo a real publisher/subscriber edge). The hybrid suppression test asserts
exact entity counts against a hardcoded expected set that did not include
it, so it failed with an extra app.

Add engine-temp-monitor to the expected app set and launch its bound node
(temp_monitor) alongside ALL_DEMO_NODES so the manifest app links to a live
runtime node and reaches online state.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): resolve metrics.source across RMWs via single-publisher fallback

metrics.source was resolved only by matching the sample's publisher GID
against the /diagnostics endpoint GIDs from the ROS graph. That match is
RMW dependent: on rmw_fastrtps_cpp both are the DDS GUID and match, but on
rmw_cyclonedds_cpp the message publisher_gid is a DDS instance handle, not
the endpoint GUID, so it never matches and source was always omitted there.

Add an RMW-agnostic fallback: when exactly one publisher exists on
/diagnostics, any sample on it must have come from that publisher, so
attribute it without relying on GID comparison. This resolves the common
case (one producer, e.g. greenwave_monitor) on every RMW. Per-sample
attribution across several simultaneous /diagnostics publishers still needs
an RMW whose message GID equals the endpoint GID; on an RMW without that,
a sample from one of several publishers is left unattributed (omitted)
rather than guessed. No RMW is special-cased - the code path is identical
everywhere and resolves more or less depending on what the RMW exposes.

The source-resolution unit tests now assert the RMW-agnostic invariant
(source is never the wrong publisher; single-publisher cases resolve on
both RMWs; the clear-on-unresolved case uses two publishers to make the
unattributable sample deterministic). Verified green under both
rmw_fastrtps_cpp and rmw_cyclonedds_cpp, unit and greenwave integration.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration_tests): drop rclpy.parameter_client for Humble compatibility

test_graph_provider_greenwave and test_graph_provider_stale imported
rclpy.parameter_client.AsyncParameterClient to live-tune a demo node's
publish_rate mid-suite. That module only exists on Jazzy+, so both test
files fail to even load on Humble ("No module named
'rclpy.parameter_client'"), failing the whole suite before a single test
runs.

Replace it with a direct rcl_interfaces/srv/SetParameters service client
against the target node's own set_parameters service - the same mechanism
AsyncParameterClient wraps internally, using only core rclpy/rcl_interfaces
APIs available on every supported distro. Behavior is unchanged: same
service name, same request/response shape, same synchronous wait-then-spin
pattern.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(graph_provider): wait for DDS discovery in source-resolution tests

metrics.source resolves via a fresh get_publishers_info_by_topic query
against the plugin node's graph cache, matched by publisher GID. Both the
unit tests and the greenwave acceptance test published a message and
asserted the resolved source right after a fixed spin+sleep, racing DDS
discovery: under CI latency the message can be processed before its
publisher's endpoint is visible in the graph cache, so source is (correctly)
omitted and the assertion flakes.

Add a bounded wait that spins and re-checks get_publishers_info_by_topic
until the expected publisher(s) are actually discovered, with a loud timeout
failure instead of a longer fixed sleep, and apply it before publishing the
message each test asserts on. The unresolved half of the clear-on-unresolved
test needs no wait, since a bogus GID never matches by construction. Extend
the acceptance test's poll to wait for metrics.source specifically, since it
can lag the edge's first active sample by a discovery cycle.

Each test still proves exactly what it did before: per-message GID
resolution across two simultaneous publishers, clearing on an unresolved
later sample while freshness still advances, and resolution to the
publisher's real fully-qualified name.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs(gateway): document remove_sampler caller-blocking contract

Document that ResourceSamplerRegistry::remove_sampler() blocks until
any in-flight invocation of that sampler callable returns. Callers
(e.g. PluginManager::disable_plugin, which holds plugins_mutex_ for
the duration of the call) must not hold a lock that the sampler
callable could itself need to acquire, or the two deadlock. The only
in-tree sampler callable today (graph_provider's x-medkit-graph
sampler) takes no such lock, so this is currently safe; the comment
protects a future plugin author who adds one that does.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): sharpen config validation warnings

Reorder the per-function override loop in load_parameters so an
unrecognized field name is always reported as unrecognized, regardless
of its value's JSON type. Previously a field that was both unknown and
given a non-numeric value hit the numeric type check first and warned
"expected a number", masking the more useful diagnosis that the field
name itself was never going to apply. The field-name recognition gate
now runs before any value-type check; a recognized field still reaches
its own type-specific validation exactly as before.

Also warn when a GLOBAL (non-override) plugin config value is present
with the wrong JSON type instead of silently falling back to the
default with no signal, matching the per-function override behavior.
An absent key remains silent, since absence is normal.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs: document robustness fields and update stale docs

Documents publisher_count, rate_ambiguous, multi_publisher_rate, and
stale_grace_sec, and fixes remaining stale docs (drop-rate caveat, timestamp
precision, the worked example, producer contract, last_seen).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): warn on invalid config overrides and guard shutdown

An override with an unknown field name or a wrong value type now warns instead
of being dropped silently. introspect() gets a shutdown guard.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): defend against multi-publisher rate inflation

frame_rate_msg is a topic-level rate summed over all publishers, so a duplicate
publisher inflates it. Each edge reports publisher_count and rate_ambiguous;
multi_publisher_rate (annotate/suppress) controls the response.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): monotonic freshness clock and stateless stale-grace

Freshness age uses a monotonic clock so a backward clock step cannot mask a
dead topic. A configurable stale_grace_sec debounces a single late sample; the
verdict is a stateless function of age, window, and grace.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs: document the graph provider plugin

Adds a tutorial, config reference, and troubleshooting entry, and corrects the
API reference and design doc to match the reworked behaviour.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration_tests): drive real greenwave_monitor through the gateway

Adds suites that feed real /diagnostics metrics through the gateway HTTP
endpoint: metrics path, staleness, cyclic subscriptions over SSE, and function
scoping.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): resolve real metrics.source from the publisher

Resolves the /diagnostics publisher node name by GID match instead of a
hardcoded literal, and omits the field when the sample cannot be attributed.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(graph_provider): set x-medkit-graph schema_version to 2.0.0

The wire contract changed (error_reason values, metrics_status semantics).
The version literal becomes a named constant.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): anchor the negotiation topic filter to path segments

Substring matching wrongly dropped real topics like /nitros_bridge/data. The
filter now matches nitros as a full path segment and _supported_types as a
trailing segment.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
refactor(graph_provider): remove the never-executed stale-topic path

Both callers disabled it, so the fault-manager correlation never ran.
Removing it drops ros2_medkit_msgs as a dependency of this package.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): apply per-function config overrides and bound state

Per-function overrides were delivered nested and silently dropped; they now
apply. Config values are validated. last_seen_by_app is bounded and the
write-only graph cache is removed.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(graph_provider): replace the status model with data freshness

Removes the global diagnostics-seen flag that reported healthy systems as
broken. metrics_status is now pending / active / error(metrics_stale), and an
edge is broken only when its metrics went stale.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): remove plugin samplers on teardown and drain in-flight calls

A cyclic-subscription sampler captures its plugin instance. The sampler
registry now drops a plugin's samplers when the plugin is torn down and drains
any call already running, so a tick cannot run against a freed plugin.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration_tests): add engine temperature monitor demo node

Gives the demo stack a real publisher/subscriber pair on one topic inside one
Function, so dataflow-graph resources actually produce an edge.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(log_bridge): wait for /rosout discovery before the first log

The integration test used a fixed 1s sleep to let the bridge connect, then
published a single ERROR log in test_01. On a slow or loaded machine (seen on
the lyrical CI job) the bridge had not matched the test's /rosout publisher
within 1s, so the first log was dropped before the subscription existed and
its fault never appeared - test_01 failed while the later tests passed
because discovery had completed by then.

Replace the fixed sleep with an active wait on the matched subscription
count, the same pattern the diagnostic_bridge and action_status_bridge
integration tests already use.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test: isolate every integration launch test on its own DDS domain

The add_launch_test integration tests in fault_manager, diagnostic_bridge,
fault_reporter, action_status_bridge and log_bridge did not set
ROS_DOMAIN_ID, so they all ran on the default domain 0. Under parallel
ctest they discovered each other's nodes: the log_bridge fault manager
picked up a fault from the action_status_bridge test node, and the timing
shift made test_01_error_log_creates_attributed_fault fail intermittently.
Only ros2_medkit_integration_tests isolated its launch tests.

Add a medkit_add_launch_test wrapper that registers a launch test and
assigns it a domain in one call, and route every launch test through it, so
a launch test can no longer be added without isolation. fault_reporter had
no range at all, so give it one.

Reallocate the domain table so the pools are disjoint and the glob-grown
integration_tests pool gets headroom: reclaim the slack in the fixed beacon
pools (param_beacon and topic_beacon each used 1 of 10, now 5 each), move
fault_reporter/log_bridge/action_status_bridge into 110-119, and grow
integration_tests to 130-219 (90 slots, 74 used). graph_provider (120-129)
and opcua (220-229) are unchanged.

Three tests also hardcoded a domain that overrode the injected one and
bypassed the table. The fault_manager launch tests test_rosbag_integration
and test_rosbag_entity_scope forced ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42/43, which collided
with the gateway gtests assigned 42 and 43. The gateway test_fault_manager
gtest forced 99 as a manual workaround for the fault_manager launch tests
running on domain 0. Drop all three overrides so each test inherits its
CMake-assigned domain; keep the ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY settings.

Closes #550

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): consistent parameter-config error surface (list vs get) and drop dead classify fallback (#543)

* fix(gateway): consistent parameter-config error surface and drop dead classify fallback

List configurations now flags itself partial and names unavailable backing
nodes instead of silently returning a shrunken 200, matching the 503 the
single-parameter GET returns for the same node outage (#541). The dead
string-matching fallback in the parameter-error classifier is removed and
extracted into a testable unit; a NONE-coded failure now maps to 500, never a
400 misclassification (#542).

Closes #541
Closes #542

* fix(gateway): scope list unavailable_nodes to 503, home classifier in core

Only a genuine 503 availability failure names a backing node "unavailable"
and keeps the list partial; a hard shutdown/internal failure now fails the
request instead of mislabeling the node behind a partial 200 (matches GET).
Move parameter_error_classification.cpp into gateway_core so its neutral
core header's symbol comes from the core lib, not the ROS adapter layer.

* fix(gateway): keep answering nodes on partial config list, rank all-down failure

A non-503 backing-node failure no longer fails the whole list and discards the
nodes that answered; the list stays 200 partial, keeps their parameters, and
names the failed node (503-class in unavailable_nodes, others in failed_nodes).
Only when no node answers does the request fail, folding through the severity
accumulator so a mixed down+internal outage returns 503 to match GET. Docs, DTO
comment and the classification/precedence test comments corrected accordingly.

* test(integration): make param-service config reads wait for readiness

The /configurations endpoints read a node's ROS 2 parameter service, which
returns 503 until that service is up. The lag is small without instrumentation
but grows under the TSan job, where the lidar-sensor service was still 503 more
than 15s after discovery finished. Tests that did a single GET (or polled with a
short timeout) on these endpoints failed intermittently there.

Add PARAM_SERVICE_TIMEOUT (90s, generous for the sanitizer slowdown; a longer
timeout costs nothing on the passing path since the poll returns as soon as the
endpoint answers) and gate every param-service config read on readiness:
- test_scenario_config_management, test_configuration_api: setUp waits for the
  configurations endpoint before each test.
- test_scenario_discovery_manifest, test_openapi_response_drift: poll the
  endpoint instead of asserting 200 on a single early GET.

* test(integration): cache param-service readiness across the config-test setUp

The per-test setUp polled the configurations endpoint up to
PARAM_SERVICE_TIMEOUT. Readiness is monotonic, but with the poll in setUp a
class of N tests paid the timeout N times, so a genuinely dead service (e.g.
9 tests x 90s) blew the ctest job budget and died on a timeout kill instead of
a readable assertion. Cache readiness on the class: only the first test polls;
the rest return immediately, and the first timeout marks the class dead so the
remaining tests fail fast.

---------

Co-authored-by: Bartosz Burda <bartoszburda93@gmail.com>

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(gateway): cover the trigger subscriber defer-before-wiring path

Add a gateway_ros2 GTest for TriggerTopicSubscriber, which had no direct unit
coverage (the core manager tests use a mock transport). It wires a real
Ros2SubscriptionExecutor and a publisher and asserts: subscribe() before the
executor is wired does not throw and parks the handle in pending; after wiring,
one retry tick turns it into a live slot that delivers a published sample; and
set_subscription_executor is set-once (null and a later different executor are
ignored). A friend test-access shim reaches the private retry hook and the
pending_/live_ maps.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): enforce set-once on the trigger subscription executor

set_subscription_executor() stored the pointer with a plain atomic store, so a
second call could overwrite it or set it to null. That is unsafe: live
subscription slots keep the executor they were created on and tear down through
it, so swapping in a different executor would orphan them (destroy via a wrong
or already-destroyed executor). Wire exactly once with compare_exchange: reject
null, and ignore a later re-set to a different executor with a warning. Update
the doc comment to match.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs(gateway): correct the set_subscription_executor contract comment

The comment still described the old behaviour (executor nullable "to detach";
subscribe() throws when unwired). subscribe() now queues the handle as pending
when the executor is not wired yet, and the executor is set once and never
cleared. Update the doc to match: set once on the main thread, read atomically
off the lock, and unwired subscribe() defers to the retry path.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): build the live trigger entry before the commit lock

subscribe() and retry_pending_subscriptions() built the LiveEntry (which owns
the subscription slot) inside the commit lock. If populating it or inserting
into live_ threw bad_alloc, the entry - and its slot - were destroyed while
mutex_ was still held, and ~Ros2SubscriptionSlot posts a run_sync destroy that
blocks on the worker, which is itself waiting on mutex_ to run a sample
callback: a self-deadlock bounded only by the 30s run_sync deadline, freezing
the whole subscription worker.

Build and populate the entry before taking the lock (matching the
old_slot/slots_to_drop discipline); under the lock only move it into live_. A
throwing insert then unwinds the entry after the lock releases. On the
not-committed path the entry's destructor drops the slot at scope exit, off the
lock. The retry commit also now inserts before erasing pending_, so a throwing
insert leaves the handle pending for a later retry instead of losing it.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): stop the REST server before freeing the subscription executor

At teardown, main.cpp freed sub_exec before ~GatewayNode stopped the REST
server, so an httplib handler already inside subscribe()/unsubscribe() could
dereference the freed subscription executor - a use-after-free. The window is
widened because subscribe() now resolves the topic type off the lock via
get_topic_names_and_types(). The data provider has the same exposure on the
/data path.

Stop and join the REST server as the first teardown step so no handler thread
can be mid-call when the executor is freed. stop_rest_server() is now public
and idempotent; ~GatewayNode still calls it as a no-op.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration): cache param-service readiness across the config-test setUp

The per-test setUp polled the configurations endpoint up to
PARAM_SERVICE_TIMEOUT. Readiness is monotonic, but with the poll in setUp a
class of N tests paid the timeout N times, so a genuinely dead service (e.g.
9 tests x 90s) blew the ctest job budget and died on a timeout kill instead of
a readable assertion. Cache readiness on the class: only the first test polls;
the rest return immediately, and the first timeout marks the class dead so the
remaining tests fail fast.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): defer trigger subscriptions when the executor is unwired

subscribe() previously logged ERROR and threw when the subscription executor
was not yet wired. That path is normal, not exceptional: persistent triggers
are restored in the GatewayNode constructor and the REST server (also started
there) can take a POST /triggers, both before main.cpp wires the executor - so
a restart with persistent data triggers spammed ERROR logs, and a POST in that
window returned 5xx for a valid request. Treat an unwired executor as a
transient startup condition: queue the handle as pending (now carrying the
caller's requested msg_type) and let the retry timer, which only fires after
spin, create the slot on its first tick.

Also move topic-type resolution out of mutex_ in both subscribe() and
retry_pending_subscriptions(): get_topic_names_and_types() takes the rmw graph
locks, and holding mutex_ across it stalled every sample dispatch on the worker
(each takes mutex_) for the query's duration. The commit phase already
re-checks the world under the lock, so resolving off the lock is safe.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration): make param-service config reads wait for readiness

The /configurations endpoints read a node's ROS 2 parameter service, which
returns 503 until that service is up. The lag is small without instrumentation
but grows under the TSan job, where the lidar-sensor service was still 503 more
than 15s after discovery finished. Tests that did a single GET (or polled with a
short timeout) on these endpoints failed intermittently there.

Add PARAM_SERVICE_TIMEOUT (90s, generous for the sanitizer slowdown; a longer
timeout costs nothing on the passing path since the poll returns as soon as the
endpoint answers) and gate every param-service config read on readiness:
- test_scenario_config_management, test_configuration_api: setUp waits for the
  configurations endpoint before each test.
- test_scenario_discovery_manifest, test_openapi_response_drift: poll the
  endpoint instead of asserting 200 on a single early GET.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(integration): poll for param service readiness in manifest config test

test_17_app_configurations_endpoint did a single GET on
/apps/lidar-sensor/configurations, which reads the node's ROS 2 parameter
service. That service can be briefly unavailable just after discovery, and
the endpoint returns 503 until it is ready, so the single GET intermittently
failed (seen on the lyrical runner). Poll the endpoint until it responds
instead of asserting on one early request.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): route trigger subscriptions through the shared subscription executor (#548)

TriggerTopicSubscriber created its per-trigger GenericSubscriptions directly
on the main gateway node, so their callbacks were dispatched by the shared
multi-threaded main executor. unsubscribe()/shutdown() reset those
subscriptions assuming GenericSubscription destruction drains in-flight
callbacks; rclcpp gives no such guarantee. At teardown a callback could still
be running on an executor thread (deserializing via the subscriber's
serializer, reading captured strings) while the subscription and those strings
were destroyed on the main thread - a data race flagged by CI TSan and an
intermittent test_triggers_data failure.

Route every trigger subscription through the existing Ros2SubscriptionExecutor
(the isolated single-worker path that /data already uses). Subscriptions are
now created, destroyed, and dispatched on that one worker via
Ros2SubscriptionSlot, so a destroy can never race an in-flight callback and
executor teardown drains any queued callback before the subscriber's state is
torn down.

- TriggerTopicSubscriber: hold a non-owning Ros2SubscriptionExecutor and store
  each live subscription as a Ros2SubscriptionSlot. Slot create/destroy go
  through run_sync, which posts to the worker and blocks; the trigger callback
  takes mutex_, so run_sync must never run under mutex_ or it deadlocks against
  a worker callback waiting on that mutex. subscribe/unsubscribe/shutdown/retry
  are restructured so all map bookkeeping stays under mutex_ while every slot
  create/destroy happens strictly outside it. Create-then-insert re-checks the
  world under the lock (shutdown flag; pending marker still present) and drops
  the just-created slot outside the lock if it changed. Fail loudly when no
  executor is wired instead of falling back to the racy node path.
- GatewayNode: set_trigger_subscription_executor() wires the executor;
  shutdown_trigger_subscriber() drains and destroys the subscriptions.
- main.cpp: wire the executor after it is built and call
  shutdown_trigger_subscriber() before sub_exec.reset() so the slots are torn
  down while the executor is still alive.
- Drop trigger_topic_subscriber.cpp from the naked-subscription allowlist and
  update the subscription-architecture design doc.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(fault_manager): empty explicit snapshot entry is an opt-out

A fault code present in fault_specific or matched by a pattern no longer
falls through to entity-default capture when its topic list is empty -
that is an explicit "capture nothing" for the code.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): harden entity freeze-frame capture

Run plugin capture on a dedicated worker so a slow list_data/x-plc-data
read cannot stall the shared subscription executor. Gate both capture
paths on live values (no {} / all-null rows), make the item parser total
for non-string ids, and bound the once-per-code warn set.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(fault_manager): skip non-FQN sources in entity-default capture

A bare plugin entity id parsed as (name, ns="/") could match an
unrelated root-namespace node of the same name and freeze-frame its
topics. Also document and pin the gateway frame retention semantics:
kept across clear, overwritten on every re-confirm.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): serve fault detail for plugin entities without a FaultProvider

Plugins that report via ReportFault only (s7comm, modbus) got a 404 from
the per-entity fault detail, hiding the fault manager's freeze-frames.
Fall through to the shared scoped listing instead.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): freeze-frame fallback via in-process x-plc-data dispatch

Plugins without a DataProvider (the commercial PLC bridges) serve live
values only through their registered routes, so entity freeze-frames
came out empty. Dispatch the owning plugin's x-plc-data route in-process
at fault confirm, gated on connected + non-empty items.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): route entity freeze-frame through Ros2SubscriptionSlot

The zero-config freeze-frame capture created a naked create_subscription on
the main node, tripping the issue #375 regression gate. Subscribe via the
shared Ros2SubscriptionExecutor instead (wired in main once the executor
exists), and update the unit test to drive the slot path.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
feat: zero-config freeze-frame - capture the faulting entity's own data by default

Fault manager: when no snapshot config matches a fault code, capture the
reporting source node's own published topics (snapshots.entity_default,
default on). Gateway: on confirm of a plugin-entity fault, snapshot the
entity's current DataProvider values and merge them into the fault detail
(entity_freeze_frame.enabled, default on). Explicit config always wins.

Closes #537

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
test(gateway): prove parameter error precedence at handler level

Replace the accumulator-only unit tests with ConfigHandlers::get_configuration
tests against a live GatewayNode (unavailable, unresponsive and reachable
backing nodes, both iteration orders) and move ParameterErrorAccumulator back
into the .cpp anonymous namespace so no test-only surface leaks from the header.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): rank multi-node parameter errors by severity

Among distinct non-404 failures the last one folded won, so a
partially-broken aggregated entity surfaced 503 or 500 depending on
node iteration order. Rank 503 > other 5xx > non-404 4xx > 404 and
keep the first failure at the winning rank.

data.author: Michal Faferek
data.message:
fix(gateway): non-404 parameter errors win over NOT_FOUND across nodes

The multi-node GET probe overwrote last_result on every failure, so a
NOT_FOUND from a later node masked a timeout/unavailable from an earlier
one and the client got 404 instead of 503. Fold failures through
ParameterErrorAccumulator so the surfaced error is order independent.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): preserve pre-write defaults, split cache caps, harden shutdown

- Separate the cache caps: the AsyncParametersClient cache keeps a moderate cap
  (kMaxParamClientCacheSize, heavy entries) while the default-value caches use a
  much larger cap (kMaxDefaultsCacheSize, light entries). Evicting a client is
  transparent (the next query rebuilds it); evicting a default is not, so its cap
  is large enough to make eviction exceptional.

- Preserve reset-to-default across eviction: set_parameter records a parameter's
  pre-write value (from its existing pre-read, so no extra round trip) in a
  dedicated pre_write_values_ cache that get_default and list_defaults prefer over
  the first-seen snapshot. Without this, evicting and re-seeding a node's defaults
  could rebase "default" to a current (already-overwritten) value, making
  reset-to-default a silent no-op.

- Emit a throttled WARN when a default-value cache evicts an entry, via a new
  optional on-evict callback on BoundedLruCache.

- Harden shutdown(): on the degraded path (spin lock not acquired within the
  timeout) block until the bounded in-flight spin releases before destroying the
  cached clients, so their rcl entities on param_node_ are never freed while a
  spin may still reference them.

Tests: transparent client rebuild after eviction; evicted defaults are re-fetched
(not reported missing); get_default returns the pre-write value after a set;
recency refresh on replace; on-evict callback. Adds a default-value cache size
accessor.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
refactor(gateway): drop default-constructible Value requirement in BoundedLruCache

BoundedLruCache::put used entries_[key], which default-constructs the mapped
Entry (and so requires Value to be default-constructible). Switch to
insert_or_assign so the cache works with any movable Value, with the same
insert-or-replace semantics and the same recency/eviction behaviour.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): bound parameter transport per-node caches with LRU eviction

Ros2ParameterTransport kept two caches keyed by node name - the
AsyncParametersClient cache and the default-value cache - that gained one
entry per distinct node name ever queried and were never evicted at runtime
(param_clients_ was only cleared at shutdown; default_values_ was never
cleared at all). On a long-lived gateway facing a churning graph this grows
without bound and leaks memory.

Back both caches with a new BoundedLruCache<Key, Value> (header-only, LRU by a
monotonic access counter, not internally locked - the caller holds the existing
clients_mutex_ / defaults_mutex_), capped at 256 entries with least-recently-used
eviction. The negative cache was already bounded; this extends the same
discipline to the other two.

Move get_param_client into the spin lock in list_parameters, matching
get_parameter and set_parameter, so creating or LRU-evicting an
AsyncParametersClient (which mutates param_node_'s entity set) is serialised with
spin_for()'s spin on param_node_ under spin_mutex_. Without this an eviction on
one thread could destroy an rcl client mid-spin on another thread.

Add a BoundedLruCache unit test and a transport-level test asserting the client
cache stays at its cap across many distinct node names.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): race-free node read in spin_for + memoize genuine SUCCESS-empty defaults (#531)

Two post-review polish items on the async parameter transport:

1. Data race on param_node_ in spin_for (real UB on shutdown's degraded
   path). spin_for read the param_node_ member twice without a lock, relying
   on spin_mutex_ to serialise against shutdown(). But shutdown() resets
   param_node_ anyway if it cannot acquire spin_mutex_ within kShutdownTimeout,
   racing an in-flight spin's read of the same shared_ptr instance. Copy the
   node once under clients_mutex_ (the lock shutdown() holds when it resets
   param_node_) and spin the local copy - synchronised read, and the node
   stays alive for the whole spin.

2. cache_default_values now memoizes a genuine SUCCESS-empty. The refactor had
   made both the TIMEOUT and SUCCESS-empty branches skip caching to avoid the
   empty-map poison, but only TIMEOUT needs that. A SUCCESS-empty (zero-param
   node, or a responsive node returning an empty set) is a stable fact and is
   safe to cache; not caching it re-ran a full round trip under spin_mutex_ on
   every get_default/list/reset and made get_default return NO_DEFAULTS_CACHED
   instead of NOT_FOUND. Cache the (possibly empty) map on both SUCCESS
   branches; keep no-cache ONLY on TIMEOUT/INTERRUPTED (poison-avoidance).

Adds a test proving a responsive-empty node memoizes its empty defaults
(get_default -> NOT_FOUND, and a second call answers from the cache without
re-round-tripping even when the node is then blocked).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): switch to AsyncParametersClient for explicit timeout detection, fixes empty-vs-timeout false positive (#531)

Root cause of the residual false positive: SyncParametersClient collapses a
SUCCESS-with-empty-result and a TIMEOUT into the same empty vector, so the
earlier "empty response when names were requested == timeout" heuristics
wrongly negative-cached and 503'd a HEALTHY node that legitimately answered
get_parameters with an empty result (e.g. a param undeclared/raced between
list and get).

Replace SyncParametersClient with AsyncParametersClient + an explicit
spin_for() helper (free-function rclcpp::spin_until_future_complete over
param_node_, bounded by service_timeout). rclcpp::FutureReturnCode now makes
the distinction unambiguous, applied uniformly to every round trip:
  TIMEOUT     -> node did not answer: mark_node_unavailable + 503
  SUCCESS     -> future.get(); the result may legitimately be EMPTY -> handle
                 without marking (get -> NOT_FOUND / list -> success=[])
  INTERRUPTED -> shutting down: SHUT_DOWN, do not mark

Removes the throw-catch and empty-as-timeout heuristics and the now-redundant
per-name fallback loops (the batch result on SUCCESS is authoritative). set:
empty results on SUCCESS is a node-side anomaly (INTERNAL_ERROR, no mark), not
a timeout. cache_default_values never caches on TIMEOUT (no empty-map poison)
and never marks on SUCCESS. The free-function spin needs no persistent-executor
lifecycle, integrating cleanly with the existing param_node_ teardown (no
SIGABRT); still serialised by spin_mutex_.

Tests: add the discriminating responsive-empty coverage (get_parameters
answers with an empty vector while responsive) asserting NOT_FOUND / success=[]
AND is_node_available==true - proven RED against the sync code, GREEN with the
async refactor. Existing timeout / recovery / ttl=0 tests kept. Docs updated.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): detect param round-trip timeouts via empty responses, not just throws (#531)

Core rclcpp-semantics bug: SyncParametersClient::get_parameters and
set_parameters do NOT throw on timeout - they return an EMPTY vector. Only
list_parameters throws. So the mark-on-timeout catch blocks added earlier
only ever fired for list_parameters; the get/set/cache timeout paths were
masked (returned 500 or success=[] with no negative-cache), leaving #531
live on those paths - fully live on writes.

Discriminator: an empty response when names WERE requested = the round-trip
timed out (a responsive node returns one entry per requested name / one
SetParametersResult per param).

- get_parameter: empty get after a found name -> TIMEOUT (503) + negative
  cache, not INTERNAL_ERROR (500).
- set_parameter: split empty results (write timeout -> TIMEOUT/503 + cache,
  at-least-once caveat) from !successful (legit read-only/type/invalid
  rejection). Pre-read get is now genuinely best-effort (log + continue).
- list_parameters op: all-empty-after-names -> TIMEOUT (503), not a
  misleading success=[].
- cache_default_values: do NOT cache an empty defaults map on timeout - that
  permanently poisoned default_values_ (never invalidated) so get_default/
  reset returned NOT_FOUND forever even after recovery. Leave uncached +
  negative-cache so a post-TTL request retries.
- Bound both per-name fallback loops under one shared deadline (~1x timeout
  total, was N x timeout). remaining passed as duration<double> so it does
  not bind the protected nanoseconds get_parameters overload.

Tests: add a fixture whose node answers list but blocks get/set, giving the
previously-absent get/set regression coverage (get-empty, set-empty,
list-op main-round-trip get-empty, and TTL recovery incl. no defaults
poison). ttl=0 cap test now asserts error class (timing-independent, no
sanitizer flake). Verified base=RED (get/set hang, SIGKILLed mid-run) /
fixed=GREEN.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): make list_parameters cap TTL-independent + genuinely-gating e2e (#531)

Fix 1 (important): the list_parameters single-round-trip cap short-circuited
on is_node_unavailable(), which is always false when negative_cache_ttl_sec
== 0 (a documented "disabled" value) - so with the negative cache disabled
the cap silently broke, list_parameters did a second round-trip and held
spin_mutex_ ~2x timeout, reintroducing the concurrent-healthy-node 503
regression. cache_default_values now returns bool (true when the node's own
round-trip failed/timed out), and list_parameters short-circuits on that
TTL-independent signal instead. Adds a ttl=0 unit test proving the cap holds.

Fix 2 (important): the e2e was vacuous - it passed against the unfixed
transport, because the shared spin_mutex_ + acquisition timeout already let
/health through under concurrency at base. Redesigned so the first test is a
single FRESH /configurations GET on an uncontended, not-yet-cached node: at
base it hangs forever (no acquisition-timeout rescue) -> client timeout ->
fail; fixed it returns 503 in ~2s. Verified base=RED / fixed=GREEN. The
concurrency + /health check is kept only as an honestly-labelled secondary
smoke test (it does not gate the hang). Docstrings corrected.

Fix 3 (minor): describe_parameters (non-essential descriptor data) in
get_parameter now has its own try/catch - a describe timeout after a good
value read degrades gracefully (empty descriptors) instead of discarding the
value and negative-caching the node.

Fix 4 (minor): comment at the set_parameters timeout catch noting a 503 does
not guarantee the set did not apply (response may be lost); clients re-read.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): map param round-trip timeout to 503 (node unavailable), not 500 (#531)

The 4 inner catches around the remote SyncParametersClient round-trips
rethrew into each operation's outer catch, which set INTERNAL_ERROR ->
config_handlers maps that to HTTP 500. A discoverable-but-unresponsive
node timing out is a node-availability failure and must surface as 503.
Each catch now negative-caches the node and returns ParameterErrorCode::
TIMEOUT (which classify_error_code maps to 503, ERR_X_MEDKIT_ROS2_NODE_
UNAVAILABLE) with a consistent message, instead of rethrowing.
cache_default_values is untouched: its rethrow is caught by its own outer
catch, which is what lets list_parameters short-circuit to
SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (also 503).

Adds a component test pinning that get_parameter() against an
unresponsive node returns a 503-class code (TIMEOUT/SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE),
never INTERNAL_ERROR.

Also hardens the e2e (test_param_service_hang): the release-barrier wait
now catches threading.BrokenBarrierError and fails cleanly instead of
erroring. Strengthens the unresponsive_param_node comment explaining why
rclcpp::shutdown() must precede executor.cancel() (the blocking
list_parameters callback loops on rclcpp::ok(), so cancel-first would
deadlock) - order unchanged, only the comment.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(gateway): widen /health bound for sanitizer CI + fix executor comment (#531)

Raise the /health-stays-responsive assertion's client timeout and elapsed
bound from 5s to 30s. Pre-fix this call was a true infinite hang, so any
bound well under the 120s CTest timeout distinguishes fixed from broken;
30s removes the flake risk under TSan/ASan CI (both required-green), which
slow this thread/lock-heavy path enough to inflate the ~2s round trip past
5s while the fix is present. The /configurations bounds and the 8-way
concurrency setup are unchanged.

Also correct the demo node's MultiThreadedExecutor comment: the gateway's
Ros2ParameterTransport serializes all parameter round trips behind a single
process-wide spin_mutex_, so only one ~/list_parameters RPC is ever in
flight at the node and a SingleThreadedExecutor would behave identically.
The concurrency under test lives in the gateway's std::async fan-out, not
in ROS-service dispatch at the demo node.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(gateway): e2e proof that an unresponsive parameter node cannot hang the REST API (#531)

Adds a launch_testing feature test plus a dedicated demo node
(unresponsive_param_node) whose parameter services are discoverable but
never reply. Proves the actual user-facing symptom is fixed: GET
.../configurations against such a node returns a bounded 503 instead of
hanging, and - the critical proof - GET /health keeps answering within a
short bound even while several concurrent /configurations calls are stuck
against the unresponsive node, instead of the whole REST API freezing
until restart.

Unit/component coverage (test_ros2_parameter_transport.cpp) already
proves Ros2ParameterTransport itself bounds every SyncParametersClient
call; this closes the gap by exercising the same scenario through a real
gateway process and HTTP worker pool.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): cap list_parameters spin_mutex hold at one round-trip (#531)

list_parameters() held the global spin_mutex_ across two bounded
round-trips against an unresponsive node - cache_default_values() then
the main list/get - for a worst case of ~2x service_timeout_sec_. That
exceeds the acquisition margin try_acquire_spin_lock() grants other
callers, so a concurrent request to a different healthy node could
spuriously fail with TIMEOUT.

Short-circuit right after cache_default_values(): if it just marked the
node unavailable, return SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE immediately instead of
paying a second round-trip. Caps the hold at ~1x service_timeout_sec_
and fails faster. Only list_parameters is affected; the other three
operations do a single round-trip already.

Also aligns the new test's TearDown with the documented
MultiThreadedExecutor order (cancel -> join -> reset) and asserts the
single-round-trip cap (elapsed < 2s). Measured first-call time drops
from ~1227ms to ~747ms.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): bound SyncParametersClient calls to service timeout so an unresponsive node cannot hang the REST API (#531)

wait_for_service() was already bounded, but the follow-up
list_parameters()/get_parameters()/describe_parameters()/set_parameters()
calls on rclcpp::SyncParametersClient passed no timeout, so rclcpp
defaulted to waiting forever. A node whose parameter service is
discoverable but unresponsive could hold spin_mutex_ and an HTTP worker
indefinitely, eventually exhausting the whole gateway thread pool.

Thread get_service_timeout() through every remote SyncParametersClient
call in list_parameters(), get_parameter(), set_parameter(), and
cache_default_values(). Scope mark_node_unavailable() to the actual
node round-trip calls (not the whole operation), so a bad client-supplied
parameter value can no longer negative-cache a healthy node.

Also removes the dead ParameterTransport::invalidate() method, which had
no callers anywhere in the codebase.
