data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
feat(opcua): AlarmConditionType state machine, poller wiring, ack/confirm ops

Wires the Part 9 AlarmConditionType subscription path into the existing
threshold-polling plugin. Builds on the event subscription primitive from
the previous commit; downstream consumers see one new YAML form
(``event_alarms:`` block) and two new SOVD operations
(``acknowledge_fault``, ``confirm_fault``).

* New header-only ``AlarmStateMachine``: pure compute_status function over
  ``EnabledState x ShelvingState x ActiveState x AckedState x ConfirmedState
  x BranchId``. Decision order documented inline; Retain is intentionally
  ignored (per Part 9 it filters ConditionRefresh visibility, not
  lifecycle). 22 unit tests cover every rule plus precedence ordering.

* ``NodeMap`` learns ``event_alarms:`` (top-level YAML sibling of
  ``nodes:``). Each entry declares ``alarm_source`` (NodeId of the source
  emitting AlarmConditionType events), ``entity_id``, ``fault_code``, and
  optional severity / message overrides. Mutually exclusive with the
  per-entry threshold ``alarm`` block; load() fails fast if both are set
  on the same node. ``find_event_alarm`` lookup serves the SOVD operation
  handlers. ``build_entity_defs`` merges event-mode entities so SOVD
  discovery surfaces them as fault-bearing even without scalar data.

* ``OpcuaPoller`` gains ``setup_event_subscriptions()`` and
  ``on_event(...)``. One dedicated subscription handles all event-mode
  alarms; the trampoline dispatches positional select-clause values
  through the state machine. ConditionRefresh fires on subscribe and on
  every reconnect (using the existing exponential-backoff path); the
  generation counter from OpcuaClient already filters callbacks captured
  from defunct subscriptions.

* Per-condition runtime is keyed by ConditionId NodeId stringForm so
  multiple instances under the same source remain distinct. Each entry
  carries the latest EventId ByteString - required for spec-compliant
  Acknowledge calls (Part 9 §5.7.3 returns BadEventIdUnknown otherwise).

* Plugin's OperationProvider lists ``acknowledge_fault`` /
  ``confirm_fault`` for any entity that has at least one event-mode
  alarm. ``execute_operation`` resolves (entity_id, fault_code) through
  the poller's lookup_condition, then invokes the inherited methods on
  AcknowledgeableConditionType (i=9111 Ack, i=9113 Confirm) with the
  tracked EventId and a LocalizedText comment. HTTP error mapping mirrors
  the existing write_value path.

* AlarmCondition events bridge through ``on_event_alarm`` to the existing
  send_report_fault / send_clear_fault wiring. Severity is mapped to the
  SOVD enum buckets (1-200 INFO, 201-500 WARN, 501-800 ERROR, 801-1000
  CRITICAL); selfpatch convention, NOT IEC 62682 - documented in the
  follow-up design doc.

Tests: 22 new state-machine unit tests (full transition table coverage
plus rule-precedence). All 144 tests in the package green; ASAN/TSAN
clean; clang-format, copyright, cppcheck, lint_cmake, xmllint all pass.

The test_alarm_server fixture and its docker integration ship in the
accompanying commit on this branch (gated OFF by default while the
ExternalProject namespace0_generated linker issue is being resolved).

Refs #386

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
feat(opcua): event subscription primitive with generation counter

Adds OpcuaClient primitives for native OPC-UA event subscription, the first
commit of issue #386 (AlarmConditionType bridge to fault_manager).
open62541pp v0.16 has no native EventFilter or event subscription support, so
this plumbs the raw open62541 C API (UA_Client_MonitoredItems_createEvent)
behind a small C++ surface that mirrors the existing data-change patterns.

Public API additions:

  * EventField + EventBrowsePath types for SimpleAttributeOperand specs.
  * EventCallback signature delivering select values plus EventType and
    SourceNode (always prepended to the filter, extracted on dispatch).
  * add_event_monitored_item / remove_event_monitored_item with
    heap-allocated CallbackContext stored as unique_ptr in OpcuaClient::Impl.
  * call_method wrapping opcua::services::call with status-mapped errors -
    needed by ConditionRefresh, Acknowledge, and Confirm in later commits.
  * current_generation() exposing a monotonic counter incremented on every
    detected disconnect (clean disconnect or transport-level drop). The
    trampoline captures a snapshot at createEvent time and drops callbacks
    whose snapshot diverges from the live counter, eliminating the late
    callback / use-after-free hazard reviewers flagged.

remove_subscriptions and disconnect now bump the generation and clear
event_callbacks before tearing down open62541pp Subscriptions, ensuring
in-flight C callbacks see a stale generation rather than a freed context.

Tests: 6 new disconnected-state tests validating the API contract and the
generation-counter ordering. End-to-end event flow against a real server
runs against the test_alarm_server fixture introduced in a later commit on
this branch (per plan v2 - in-process server tests with synthetic event
triggering are deferred to keep this commit reviewable; the docker
integration test in commit 5 covers the full path).

Refs #386

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs+ci: error code semantics, design doc fixes, regression gate hardening

Rolls up the documentation, configuration, and CI-gate changes from the
issue #375 PR review rounds.

Operator + API consumer docs:
- docs/api/rest.rst: document the three new x-medkit-* vendor error codes
  with retry guidance per code:
    x-medkit-gateway-shutdown        503, do NOT retry
    x-medkit-subscribe-failed        500, retry once with short backoff
    x-medkit-cold-wait-cap-exceeded  503, retry with exponential backoff
                                     (params.cold_wait_cap carries the cap).
  Without these, MCP / Web UI / other clients with retry-on-5xx logic
  conflate them into "503 transient, retry" and hammer a shutting-down
  gateway.
- docs/tutorials/plugin-system.rst: warning callout under PluginContext::node()
  pointing at Ros2SubscriptionSlot for plugin authors who used to call
  create_subscription directly.

Design doc fixes:
- src/ros2_medkit_gateway/design/ros2_subscription_architecture.rst:
  rewrite both "metadata-only immediately" passages (sample() flow and
  the dedicated Cold-wait cap section). The code returns a 503 + retry
  contract since the cold-wait cap landed; doc was stale.
- src/ros2_medkit_gateway/design/index.rst: max_parallel_topic_samples
  reference replaced with data_provider.max_parallel_samples (live knob
  on TopicDataProvider, not the dead DataAccessManager field).
- src/ros2_medkit_serialization/design/index.rst: NativeTopicSampler

- src/ros2_medkit_gateway/README.md: max_parallel_topic_samples references

  knobs instead.

Configuration:
- gateway_params.yaml: removed dead max_parallel_topic_samples knob;
  new subscription_executor.* and data_provider.* sections document
  cold_wait_cap, max_parallel_samples, idle_safety_net_sec, etc.

CI regression gate (scripts/check_no_naked_subscriptions.sh):
- Switched the inner scan from line-by-line grep -rEn to perl with -0777
  (slurp-as-string). A constructor split across lines (auto sub =
  node->create_subscription\n    <T>(...);) had no single line containing
  create_subscription< and slipped past the previous gate.
- Extended scan_dirs to src/ros2_medkit_fault_manager/{src,include}.
  fault_manager landed the same race-class fix in this PR (LockedSubscription

  Allowlisted snapshot_capture.cpp / .hpp explicitly with rationale.
- Hardened scan-misconfiguration paths: missing scan_dirs, no source files
  found, perl missing all exit 2 instead of silently passing the gate.
  Failure message updated to reference the correct design-doc path

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(gateway): stress + edge-case coverage from review

New and updated unit tests landed during the issue #375 PR review rounds.

Concurrency stress (regression test for the rcl hash-map race that the
SOVD provider architecture exists to fix):
- ConcurrentSampleFromMultipleThreadsDoesNotCrash bumped from 4x10 to
  16x50 with a high cold_wait_cap so the test exercises the cold-create
  race window rather than being limited by back-pressure shedding.
  Strict EXPECT_EQ(pool_size, 1u) (was EXPECT_GE) pins the deduplication
  invariant - a regression that leaks a subscription per concurrent
  caller now fails immediately.
- New ConcurrentSampleStressColdCreatePath: rotates topic names per
  iteration so every sample goes through the cold-create path (the
  actual rcl_subscription_init race site from issue #375); previous test
  hit the warm pool after the first call.
- Both tests carry a comment marking them as TSan/ASan-required to
  catch the original bug; CI sanitizer-asan and sanitizer-tsan run all
  unit tests on every push.
- Slot test: DestructorSafeWhenDestroyTaskDrainsAfterSlotFreed forces
  the deadline-after-slot-freed ordering by gating the worker behind a
  promise/future and only releasing after slot.reset(). Pins the
  move-into-task UAF fix.

API contract / partial-success:
- SampleParallelHonorsMaxParallelSamplesAndPreservesOrder: max_parallel_samples=2
  with 5 input topics forces 3 chunk iterations; pins ordering across
  chunk boundaries.
- SampleParallelEmbedsPerTopicErrorInsteadOfFailingBatch: holder thread
  saturates a cap-of-1 cold-wait slot, asserts the per-topic error is
  embedded in the result rather than failing the whole batch (matches the
  partial-success contract reviewer asked for).
- ColdWaitCapExceededReturns503: dedicated test for the 503 + retry
  contract (was metadata-only success before the contract change).

Detach + null-provider paths added in main()'s teardown:
- DataAccessManager.set_topic_data_provider_nullptr_detaches_provider
  exercises attach -> detach -> re-attach + verifies get_topic_data_provider
  returns nullptr after detach.
- DiscoveryManager.SetTopicDataProviderNullptrIsAcceptedAfterAttach
  exercises the same path indirectly via discover_components since
  RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy has no public getter.

Misc:
- test_error_info.cpp updated to use real error_codes.hpp constants
  (ERR_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, ERR_X_MEDKIT_ROS2_TOPIC_UNAVAILABLE) instead
  of a non-existent ERR_TOPIC_NOT_FOUND.
- test_ros2_subscription_executor: parameter overrides updated for the
  removed main_executor ctor argument.
- @verifies REQ_INTEROP_018 / REQ_INTEROP_019 tags added to the new
  unit tests so they show up in the SOVD verification matrix.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): production hardness from review (concurrency + lifetime + error contracts)

Bundles all production-code fixes that landed during the three review rounds
on the issue #375 SOVD provider architecture PR. Listed by review concern
class so future archaeology can find them by symptom.

Subscription lifecycle / concurrency:
- Ros2SubscriptionSlot dtor moves the subscription out of `this` into the
  posted destroy task so the rcl handle's lifetime no longer depends on
  the slot surviving run_sync's deadline (UAF window closed).
- Slot dtor detects "I am the worker thread" via Ros2SubscriptionExecutor's
  worker_thread_id() and drops the subscription inline; posting to run_sync
  from inside a worker callback (e.g. a graph callback evicting its own
  pool entry) deadlocks the worker on its own queue.
- Slot dtor is now noexcept and wraps run_sync in try/catch so OOM during
  promise/future construction cannot escape and trip std::terminate.
- Ros2SubscriptionExecutor: graph fan-out posts a single wrapper for the
  whole snapshot instead of one post per listener, so backpressure becomes
  all-or-nothing instead of half-delivered. aux_loop now waits on a CV
  with shutdown predicate (was sleep_for(graph_poll_tick)), so destruction
  returns within microseconds rather than the next 100ms tick. Watchdog
  flapping fixed: degraded_ stays sticky for the in-flight task and only
  clears when the worker is observed idle. Graph-listener removal hazard
  documented in the public header.
- Ros2SubscriptionExecutor::node() public doc rewritten with explicit
  allowed (read-only) vs forbidden (mutating) operation lists, pointing
  at the regression gate as the structural enforcement.
- Removed the unused main_executor ctor parameter; subscription node is
  always owned by the internal SingleThreadedExecutor spun from the
  worker thread.

Data path:
- sample_parallel rewritten as partial-success: per-topic recoverable
  errors (cold-wait cap, subscribe-failed) are embedded into the
  corresponding TopicSampleResult instead of failing the whole batch.
  TopicSampleResult gains optional error_code / error_message /
  error_http_status. Only ERR_X_MEDKIT_GATEWAY_SHUTDOWN remains
  batch-fatal. Concurrency is bounded by a new max_parallel_samples knob
  to stop std::async fan-out from self-DoSing under large topic lists.
- qos_for: copies publisher Deadline / Lifespan / Liveliness into the
  subscriber QoS (Cyclone DDS rejects on deadline mismatch, FastDDS
  silently never delivers); WARN logged for conflicting publisher
  contracts on the same topic.
- ROS 2 graph introspection calls (get_topic_names_and_types,
  count_publishers, etc) are now wrapped in try/catch(std::runtime_error)
  with DEBUG logging; previously every late-shutdown call could
  std::terminate the gateway. Per-topic enumeration uses `continue`
  instead of `break` so a transient rmw fault on one topic no longer
  truncates the entire result.
- Graph-change callback now captures a shared alive flag; the dtor clears
  it before remove_graph_change(), so already-queued callbacks no-op
  instead of dereferencing a dangling this. Idle-sweep timer guarded
  the same way.
- Cold-wait cap exhaustion now returns ERR_X_MEDKIT_COLD_WAIT_CAP_EXCEEDED
  (503 + retry contract) instead of metadata-only success, so retry-on-5xx
  clients can apply backoff. Three new vendor codes added to error_codes.hpp:
  x-medkit-gateway-shutdown, x-medkit-subscribe-failed,
  x-medkit-cold-wait-cap-exceeded.
- DataAccessManager preserves err.http_status: 404 keeps the original
  TopicNotAvailableException mapping, every other status raises a new
  ProviderErrorException that handlers translate back to the original
  code + HTTP status. Closes the 5xx-collapsing-to-404 contract bug.
- Handlers (data_handlers, health_handlers) inspect the tl::expected
  return from provider->sample() and forward errors via ctx_.send_error
  with the provider's code, http_status, and params instead of falling
  through to a metadata-only response.
- main.cpp: executor.spin() wrapped in try/catch so an escaping handler
  exception cannot bypass the explicit teardown block. Teardown order
  also detaches the provider from GatewayNode (set_topic_data_provider
  (nullptr)) before the local shared_ptr resets, since GatewayNode
  otherwise holds its own shared_ptr that would keep the provider alive.

Dead code / cleanup:
- Deleted Ros2TopicDataProvider::build_metadata_only_sample (zero callers,
  relic of the original cold-wait fallback).
- Deleted DataAccessManager::max_parallel_samples_ (declared, validated,
  logged - never read; live tuning lives at data_provider.max_parallel_samples
  on the provider).
- Removed unimplemented metadata_cache_cap config + metadata_cache_size
  stat (the cache was never built; the field always reported 0).
- Renamed RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy::topic_sampler_ to topic_data_provider_
  after NativeTopicSampler was absorbed into Ros2TopicDataProvider.
- Lock order documented at the top of ros2_topic_data_provider.cpp:
  pool_mtx_ before buf_mtx_, never reversed; sweep_idle_entries() is the
  only nested-lock site.
- Bumped copyright on touched files to 2026.

fault_manager:
- SnapshotCapture closes the destroy-side rcl race with a
  LockedSubscriptionGuard RAII that takes node_ops_mutex_ before resetting
  the subscription + callback group together (the create-side mutex was
  already there).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(param_beacon): bump gmock TIMEOUT from 30s to 180s for TSan runs

test_param_beacon_plugin flaked sanitizer-tsan with a ctest 30s
timeout after getting through only 3-4 of its 12 test cases.
The suite is fast under plain gcc (~4s total), but each case spins
a node for 200-400ms and TSan instrumentation inflates that 5-10x,
which pushes the full run over 30s on some CI runners.

180s comfortably covers the worst observed sanitizer slowdown while
still catching a real hang an order of magnitude before that.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(demo_nodes): sigwait-thread shutdown instead of rclcpp default handler

Integration-test CI kept cycling through a rotating 'shutdown victim'
from the demo cast (engine_temp_sensor, lidar_sensor, brake_actuator,
calibration_service, fault_manager_node, ...). Symptoms were exit code
255 with rosidl_runtime_c asserting mid-shutdown:

  Unexpected condition: string capacity was zero for allocated data! Exiting.

Root cause: the demos called rclcpp::init() with default options, which
installs an async SIGINT / SIGTERM handler that calls rclcpp::shutdown()
directly from the signal handler. That invalidates the shared rcl
context immediately, so an in-flight timer callback publishing a
sensor_msgs::msg::Temperature (or similar) message can catch the
allocator mid-teardown and tear down its header.frame_id against
freed state - hence the rosidl assert.

New pattern, encapsulated in a new helper
ros2_medkit_integration_tests/demo_node_main.hpp:

  1. Main thread blocks SIGINT / SIGTERM before any rclcpp work.
  2. rclcpp::init() is called with SignalHandlerOptions::None so rclcpp
     does NOT install its own signal handler.
  3. A dedicated thread blocks on sigwait() for SIGINT / SIGTERM with
     the inherited mask; on arrival it calls executor.cancel() to wake
     spin() from a known-good thread context.
  4. The main thread runs executor.spin(). When spin returns, the rcl
     context is still valid: the sigwait thread only canceled the
     executor, it did not call rclcpp::shutdown().
  5. Main then removes the node from the executor and resets the
     shared_ptr. Publisher / message destruction races nothing - the
     allocator and rcl context are both healthy.
  6. rclcpp::shutdown() is the very last call.

All 11 demo nodes now go through run_demo_node() from the helper.
std::set_terminate() in long_calibration_action.cpp is retained; it
covers a separate rclcpp_action mid-goal race.

Verified locally on Jazzy: test_health, test_sse, test_beacon_param
(the three previous flake victims) pass 14 / 14.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(ros2_common,data): move test publishers off the executor-spun node

TSan flagged data races on rcutils_hash_map_{get,set} between the
MultiThreadedExecutor spin thread iterating the test's gateway node
and the test body creating / destroying rclcpp::Publisher instances
on the very same node. Publishers do not need spinning, so park them
on a second, unspun publisher_node_ in the fixtures:

- Ros2TopicDataProviderTest
- Ros2SubscriptionSlotTest
- DataAccessManagerWithPublisherTest

All 15 create_publisher call sites now target the unspun node, which
removes the TSan-reported reader side without changing any assertion.
test_ros2_topic_data_provider locally: 19 / 19 pass, full gateway
suite 2970 / 2970.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(param_beacon): swallow rcl 'context invalid' in graph poll during shutdown

TSan CI's test_beacon_param flaked on a shutdown-race abort the previous
fix did not cover. ParamBeaconPlugin's poll timer calls
node_graph->get_node_names_and_namespaces() when no introspection
targets are configured; if the timer fires between the rclcpp signal
handler invalidating the context and the executor stopping, the call
throws std::runtime_error and the exception escapes the timer callback
up to std::terminate.

Wrap the call in try/catch and return early when rcl reports the
context invalid; the next tick will either find the executor stopped
or resume normally if there was a spurious race.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(ros2_common): make StatsTrackCompletedTasks tolerate race with worker_loop

run_sync's wrapper fulfills its future inside task(), which the worker
then increments tasks_completed_ for. The caller can therefore observe
a completed run_sync while stats.tasks_completed still lags by one.
The assertion raced under slower CI runners (Pixi on jazzy surfaced it
reliably). Poll stats with a short deadline instead of reading once so
the eventual-consistency window closes before we fail the test.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(discovery,data): swallow rcl 'context invalid' throws during shutdown

TSan CI caught a new shutdown-race abort on test_beacon_param:

  terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  failed to get node names: rcl node's context is invalid
  exit code -6

The refresh timer on the gateway node fires once between SIGINT arriving
(rclcpp's signal handler calls rclcpp::shutdown(), invalidating the
shared rcl context) and the main executor actually stopping. If the
timer's callback happens to be mid-run when that window opens, the
subsequent rclcpp graph queries throw std::runtime_error. Those escape
the callback, escape the executor, and std::terminate fires.

Wrap the three graph-query call sites that can realistically race
shutdown in try/catch and return an empty result on failure; callers
already treat empty lists as a valid transient state:

- RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy::discover_apps (get_node_names_and_namespaces)
- RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy::discover_services (get_service_names_and_types)
- RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy::discover_actions (get_service_names_and_types)
- Ros2TopicDataProvider::on_graph_change (get_topic_names_and_types) -
  fired from the aux thread's graph-poll tick, which keeps running
  after rclcpp::shutdown until our own shutdown_flag_ is set.

The pre-existing try/catch around get_service_names_and_types_by_node
already follows this pattern.

Verified locally on Jazzy Debug: 3790 / 3790 tests pass (gateway unit +
integration).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(ros2_common): own the subscription-node executor, move timers off it

TSan caught a second race on subscription_node_'s internal rcutils
hash map: the worker thread was destroying subscriptions under
run_sync while the gateway's MultiThreadedExecutor spin threads were
still iterating the same node's subscription list from the other side.
Sharing subscription_node_ between the gateway executor (where it was
added for callback dispatch) and the run_sync worker (where
creation / destruction happens) is the textbook violation of rcl's
single-writer rule that the whole pool-backed architecture was
supposed to prevent.

Give Ros2SubscriptionExecutor its own SingleThreadedExecutor that
exclusively owns subscription_node_. The worker thread interleaves
run_sync task dispatch with sub_executor_.spin_some() so subscription
callbacks (including any user-supplied typed / generic callbacks and
the graph-poll event) fire on the same thread that creates and
destroys the subscriptions. The gateway's main executor no longer
touches subscription_node_ at all.

Because spin_some() only runs while the worker is idle, the watchdog
and graph-event-polling ticks can no longer ride on subscription_node_
wall timers (a long-running run_sync task would starve them). Replace
both timers with a small dedicated aux thread that calls
watchdog_tick() / graph_poll_tick() on their independent cadences.
The tick functions already only touch this object's atomics and the
graph event, so running them off-thread is safe.

Verified locally: full ros2_medkit_gateway unit suite (2970 / 2970)
and the previously-flaky integration tests (test_sse + test_health,
10 / 10) pass on a Debug build.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(ros2_common): avoid UAF + rcutils race in subscription executor/slot

Sanitizer CI caught two latent issues introduced with the pool-backed
architecture:

ASan: heap-use-after-free in Ros2SubscriptionSlot::~Ros2SubscriptionSlot
  The slot stored a raw reference to the Ros2SubscriptionExecutor and
  dereferenced exec_.is_shutting_down() in its destructor. The paired
  test DestructorOnShuttingDownExecutorDoesNotCrash destroys the
  executor before the slot on purpose (the fast-path contract), so
  that call read from freed memory.

  Promote the shutdown flag to std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>>
  owned jointly by executor and any slot it created. The executor sets
  the flag to true at the top of its destructor so slots observing it
  afterwards still see 'shutting down' even when the executor itself
  is gone. shutdown_flag_ptr() exposes the shared_ptr so slots can
  copy it at construction. is_shutting_down() now loads from the
  shared_ptr so it stays meaningful for the executor's own lifetime
  too. Slot::exec_ is now a non-owning pointer, used only on the
  normal destroy path when the flag is still false.

TSan: data race on rcutils_array_list_fini between the main executor
  spin thread and ~Ros2SubscriptionExecutor. remove_node() is
  thread-safe but does not wait for the spin thread to drop its
  weak_ptr view of the node; a follow-up subscription_node_.reset()
  then races with the spin thread's cleanup of the node's internal
  rcl lists. Production main() dodges this because executor.spin() has
  already returned before sub_exec.reset(), but the test fixtures tore
  things down in the opposite order.

  Fix in every affected test fixture: cancel the main executor and
  join its spin thread BEFORE resetting sub_exec / provider, so the
  subscription node is destroyed while no one else is touching it.
  Covers test_discovery_manager, test_ros2_topic_data_provider,
  test_ros2_subscription_executor, test_ros2_subscription_slot.

Verified locally: full ros2_medkit_gateway colcon test passes
(2970/2970), including the DestructorOnShuttingDownExecutorDoesNotCrash
case under a Debug build.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(http,sse): unblock SSE chunked provider before joining server thread

jazzy-test's test_sse.TestShutdown.test_exit_codes and other integration
tests that exercise the SSE fault stream started killing the gateway
with SIGKILL (exit -9) after launch_testing's SIGINT -> SIGTERM (5s) ->
SIGKILL (10s more) budget elapsed without the process exiting. The
process was stuck in GatewayNode::stop_rest_server waiting for
server_thread_->join(), which in turn was waiting for the SSE chunked-
content-provider lambda to return.

That lambda sleeps on queue_cv_.wait_for(keepalive_interval_) and its
only wakeup signals are a new fault event, the 30s keepalive timer, or
the shutdown_flag_. shutdown_flag_ was previously only set in
~SSEFaultHandler, which does not run until the handler's owning
RESTServer is destroyed - long after stop_rest_server must have
already returned. So the 15s shutdown budget was racing a 30s keepalive
CV and losing on slower CI runners.

Add SSEFaultHandler::request_shutdown() that sets the flag and notifies
the CV under the queue mutex, and invoke it from RESTServer::stop()
before http_server_->stop(). The SSE lambda wakes, sees the flag, and
returns false so the httplib worker exits promptly; the main shutdown
path then proceeds normally. ~SSEFaultHandler reuses the same method
for idempotency.

Verified locally on Jazzy: test_sse + test_health (both previously
failing) pass cleanly, gateway exits with -15 (SIGTERM, allowed).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: CI failures from issue #375 PR

Three unrelated CI failures surfaced once the pool-backed architecture
landed on rolling and the docs / clang-tidy jobs picked up the changed
headers.

docs: Sphinx treats continuation-indented parenthetical text as a block
quote; the 'TopicDataProvider / Ros2TopicDataProvider' entry in
docs/design/ros2_medkit_gateway/index.rst (symlinked from the package
design dir) now inlines the parenthetical into the bullet line so that
'build finished with problems, 2 warnings' stops failing build-docs.

main: rolling rclcpp now aborts with
  'Node /ros2_medkit_gateway needs to be associated with an executor'
if a service client or subscription is used from a node whose executor
has already been destroyed. Stack-var destruction order in main()
destroyed the executor before the gateway node, so ~GatewayNode's
manager shutdown path tripped the check. Explicitly remove the node
from the executor and reset the shared_ptr before returning, so
~GatewayNode runs while the executor is still alive.

test_plugin_manager: 'using namespace ros2_medkit_gateway;' already
imports the namespace-level 'using json = nlohmann::json;' from
discovery/models/common.hpp. The local 'using json = nlohmann::json;'
shadowed it and tripped clang-diagnostic-shadow once clang-tidy started
running on the file (transitively changed via the plugin header
rearrangement). Drop the redundant alias and leave a note.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
refactor: delete NativeTopicSampler (absorbed by Ros2TopicDataProvider)

Removes the legacy NativeTopicSampler class entirely. Every production call
site now routes sampling through Ros2TopicDataProvider, so the rcl hash-map
race behind issue #375 can no longer be reintroduced by a fallback path.

- Drop native_sampler_ field, getter, and construction from DataAccessManager.
  get_topic_sample_native() now errors out cleanly if no provider is attached.
- Drop NativeTopicSampler fallbacks from data_handlers.cpp and gateway_node.cpp.
- Delete include/ros2_medkit_gateway/native_topic_sampler.hpp,
  src/native_topic_sampler.cpp and test/test_native_topic_sampler.cpp.
  Migrate its ThreadSafety scenarios (timeout-without-publisher, rapid-timeout-
  with-active-publisher) into test_ros2_topic_data_provider.cpp.
- Fix test_data_access_manager to wire up a Ros2TopicDataProvider in SetUp
  (matches the main() assembly); replace the get_native_sampler getter test
  with one for get_topic_data_provider.
- Remove NativeTopicSampler entries from check_no_naked_subscriptions.sh
  allowlist, design/architecture.puml and design/index.rst. The architecture
  doc now shows TopicDataProvider + Ros2TopicDataProvider + Ros2SubscriptionExecutor.

Verified: 2110/2110 unit tests pass, grep for NativeTopicSampler returns zero
production matches, CI regression gate still reports OK.

docs(design): architecture doc for ROS 2 subscription pool

Adds docs/design/ros2_medkit_gateway/ros2_subscription_architecture.rst

  Ros2SubscriptionSlot -> Ros2SubscriptionExecutor -> rclcpp.

  public API + wall-timer poll, shutdown drain semantics.

  hatch.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(observability): GET /health/subscription-pool drill-in endpoint

Per-topic snapshot of the ROS 2 subscription pool via a dedicated
endpoint to avoid bloating /health itself. Response includes one entry
per pool slot with topic, message_type, LRU rank, has_latest,
latest_ns, and last_sample_age_ms. Output is bounded (at most
max_pool_size entries).

Wiring:
- New virtual TopicDataProvider::x_medkit_pool_snapshot() -> json,
  default []. Keeps alternate transports from having to implement it.
- Ros2TopicDataProvider override walks lru_order_ under pool_mtx_ so
  callers get entries in MRU-first order with a rank index.
- HealthHandlers::handle_subscription_pool composes the response with
  the per-entry snapshot plus the aggregate counters from x_medkit_stats.
- Route registered via RouteRegistry with tag Server, operation id
  getSubscriptionPool.

Intended for diagnostics (stuck slot, unbounded growth, high age),
not for tight polling loops.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): match subscriber QoS to publisher QoS

Previously the pool's generic subscriptions were always created with
SensorDataQoS (best-effort, depth 1, volatile). That was fine for
best-effort sensor streams but had two correctness gaps:

1. Reliable publishers could still connect but delivery semantics were
   downgraded; messages delivered asynchronously could be dropped.
2. TransientLocal (latched) publishers rely on matching subscriber
   durability to replay the last message on connection. With volatile
   subscribers, the latched value was never seen - /data returned
   metadata-only for topics that should have had data immediately.

qos_for(topic) now queries publishers via get_publishers_info_by_topic
(thread-safe graph read) and derives:
- Reliable if any publisher is Reliable, else BestEffort
- TransientLocal if any publisher is TransientLocal, else Volatile
- keep_last depth 1 (pool only keeps the latest message)

Test SampleMatchesReliablePublisherQoS verifies a reliable+latched
publisher replays its last message to the provider's subscriber on
pool entry creation.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): cold-wait cap preserves httplib liveness under sample load

When many HTTP handler threads simultaneously sample() cold topics (pool
entry exists but no message has arrived yet), each blocks on the
per-entry condvar until timeout. With httplib's bounded worker pool
(typically 4-8 threads on embedded), this can saturate the pool and
starve unrelated endpoints like /health, /components, /discovery.

Mitigation: Ros2TopicDataProvider tracks concurrent_cold_waits_. When
it reaches cfg.cold_wait_cap (default 4), further callers on cold
topics return metadata-only immediately instead of blocking. Existing
waiters complete normally; warm topics always get served via the fast
path and are unaffected.

Test ColdWaitCapShedsLoad verifies that 4 concurrent cold samplers
with cap=2 produce at least 2 fast metadata-only returns under 200ms
rather than all waiting the full 1s timeout.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): idle safety net evicts long-dormant pool entries

Periodic sweep drops pool entries whose last_sample_time is older than
cfg.idle_safety_net (default 15 min). Runs on a wall timer on the
subscription node; cadence is cfg.idle_sweep_tick (default 1 min).

Motivation: a topic that is sampled once then forgotten keeps its slot
alive indefinitely under the current design. On long-lived deployments
with dynamic topic sets this accumulates slots, burning memory and DDS
endpoint state. The sweep provides a deterministic upper bound on pool
occupancy decoupled from explicit churn signals (LRU only triggers on
a miss at cap; graph-change only triggers on removed topics).

sweep_idle_entries() is public so unit tests can trigger it without
waiting for the timer. Setting cfg.idle_sweep_tick = 0 or
cfg.idle_safety_net = 0 disables the sweep entirely.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): LRU eviction when pool reaches max_pool_size

Previous behavior degraded to metadata-only when the pool was full, which
meant rare topics in a busy system stayed permanently unsampleable. The
LRU list tracks per-topic recency: hits promote to MRU via list splice,
and a miss at cap evicts the LRU entry to make room for the new slot.

Evicted entries have their shutdown flag set and CV notified before
release so any in-flight sample() on that topic unblocks promptly rather
than waiting for the full timeout.

Graph-change eviction and the destructor also maintain the LRU side
structures so they stay in sync with pool_.

Tests:
- PoolCapEvictsLruWhenFull
- HitPromotesTopicToMru (verifies the hit-promoted entry survives the
  next eviction and returns hits on subsequent samples)

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(observability): expose x-medkit-* subscription stats on /health

Surface Ros2TopicDataProvider pool stats and Ros2SubscriptionExecutor
worker/queue/watchdog stats on GET /health via vendor-extension keys:

- x-medkit-data-provider: pool_size/cap, pool hits/misses, evictions,
  type_change_events, graph_events_received, cold_wait_cap.
- x-medkit-subscription-executor: worker_alive, degraded,
  queue_depth/max/dropped, tasks_completed/failed, latency percentiles,
  current_task_age_ms, watchdog_trips.

External monitors (k8s liveness probe, Docker HEALTHCHECK, systemd
watchdog, Prometheus exporters) can trigger on
.x-medkit-subscription-executor.degraded without any deployment-specific
assumptions. Atomic reads only; /health does not block.

Wiring:
- New virtual TopicDataProvider::x_medkit_stats() -> json, default {}.
  Lets alternate transports contribute their own stats without changing
  the handler.
- Ros2TopicDataProvider override returns pool + executor stats together.
- GatewayNode exposes get_topic_data_provider() for the handler to call.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(data): add concurrent-sample race regression test

Regression gate for issue #375. Four threads hammer sample() on the same
active topic concurrently. Under the legacy NativeTopicSampler path this
raced inside rcl's internal hash map during create_generic_subscription /
destroy calls from multiple httplib handler threads; the pool-backed
Ros2TopicDataProvider funnels all subscription lifecycle through the
serial Ros2SubscriptionExecutor worker and shares the pool entry across
concurrent samplers.

The test publishes continuously in the background and expects every
sample() call to complete successfully and the pool to retain a single
entry for the topic regardless of concurrent miss attempts.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
refactor(discovery,http): migrate discovery + data handler to TopicDataProvider

DiscoveryManager::set_topic_sampler -> set_topic_data_provider, accepting
TopicDataProvider* instead of NativeTopicSampler*. RuntimeDiscoveryStrategy
stores a TopicDataProvider* internally; it only uses build_component_topic_map()
which is identical across the two interfaces.

GatewayNode::set_topic_data_provider also forwards the provider to
DiscoveryManager so the runtime strategy's topic-map refresh is wired up
after main() stands up the provider. The cache-refresh path in
GatewayNode::refresh_cache() also prefers the provider over the native
sampler.

last production sampling call site that still went through NativeTopicSampler.

Ros2SubscriptionExecutor) instead of a NativeTopicSampler.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): wire TopicDataProvider through DataAccessManager + main

Issue #375 production-path fix:

- DataAccessManager grows a TopicDataProvider setter/getter alongside the
  existing NativeTopicSampler. When the provider is set (the production
  case after main.cpp wires it up), sample paths route through the
  pool-backed Ros2TopicDataProvider and no longer call into the
  race-prone NativeTopicSampler::sample_topic. NativeTopicSampler stays
  live for tests that construct DataAccessManager in isolation and for
  discovery/graph queries (thread-safe, unrelated to the race).

- GatewayNode gains set_topic_data_provider(shared_ptr<TopicDataProvider>)
  which stores ownership and forwards the raw pointer into
  DataAccessManager.

- main.cpp stands up the chain after executor.add_node(node):
    Ros2SubscriptionExecutor -> JsonSerializer -> Ros2TopicDataProvider
  then node->set_topic_data_provider(...). Teardown drops the provider
  first (pool flush via executor), then resets sub_exec (joins worker,
  removes subscription node), then rclcpp::shutdown().

- The built-in data resource sampler in gateway_node also prefers the
  provider when available, with a fallback to NativeTopicSampler during
  the transition.

Discovery, runtime_discovery, and trigger_topic_subscriber still use
NativeTopicSampler; those call sites are graph queries and do not
trigger the rcl subscription race. They migrate in follow-up work when
NativeTopicSampler is removed.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): add pool-based sample() to Ros2TopicDataProvider

Long-lived subscription pool fixes the rcl hash-map race that was the
root cause of issue #375: concurrent sample() calls no longer create /
destroy subscriptions from httplib threads. All subscription lifecycle
runs through Ros2SubscriptionExecutor's serial worker via
Ros2SubscriptionSlot.

Pool entry per topic keeps the always-newest serialized message. First
sample creates the slot (miss); subsequent samples on the same topic
reuse the entry (hit). Concurrent samplers on the same topic share the
latest message via a per-entry condvar - no coordination needed.

Graph-change callback evicts entries for topics that have left the graph
or whose type has changed. Pool is bounded: at max_pool_size, new misses
degrade to metadata-only rather than displacing an existing entry. LRU
eviction, idle safety net, and cold-wait cap remain follow-ups.

Sample_parallel fans out via std::async.

Destructor signals every per-entry CV, drops pool entries.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): add Ros2TopicDataProvider skeleton with discovery

ROS 2 default implementation of TopicDataProvider. This revision ships
all discovery methods live (graph queries via the subscription node) but
leaves sample() / sample_parallel() returning metadata-only results; the
pool-backed sampling path lands in a follow-up commit.

Purpose: get the TopicDataProvider interface in front of callers so they
can migrate via interface reference before the pool is ready, without
regressing the legacy NativeTopicSampler path still wired into gateway
sampling. NativeTopicSampler is removed after migration + pool.

QoS conversion helpers are duplicated from native_topic_sampler.cpp; the
duplication disappears when NativeTopicSampler is deleted.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(data): add TopicDataProvider interface + extract data_types

Pure-C++ interface for the upcoming ROS 2 topic sampling infrastructure,
consumed by DataAccessManager / DiscoveryManager / RuntimeDiscovery. Uses
tl::expected<T, ErrorInfo> error convention. All methods [[nodiscard]].

Renamed from DataProvider to TopicDataProvider to avoid colliding with
the existing plugin-facing ros2_medkit_gateway::DataProvider in
providers/data_provider.hpp - the two operate at different architectural
layers (infrastructure vs. plugin delegation).

Extracted TopicInfo, TopicSampleResult, TopicDiscoveryResult from
native_topic_sampler.hpp into data/data_types.hpp. TopicDiscoveryResult
moved out of the NativeTopicSampler class body to namespace scope.

refactor: move 4 providers to domain dirs

Move log_provider, script_provider, update_provider, introspection_provider
out of include/ros2_medkit_gateway/providers/ into their domain directories
(logs/, scripts/, updates/, discovery/). Updates 24 #include lines across
gateway sources, tests, plugins, and docs.

fault_provider, operation_provider) in place - those serve a different

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(ros2_common): add Ros2SubscriptionSlot RAII handle

Standalone final class wrapping a single rclcpp subscription whose
lifecycle is serialized on the Ros2SubscriptionExecutor worker thread.
Two static factories: create_typed<MessageT> for typed subscriptions,
create_generic for runtime-typed topics.

Destructor takes the shutdown fast-path when the executor is already
shutting down (releasing on current thread, relying on rcl_node_fini
to clean up the rcl handle). Otherwise posts a bounded 30s destroy
task to the worker. No public release_without_executor escape hatch -
shrinks the API surface for future safety analysis.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(ros2_common): add Ros2SubscriptionExecutor

Serial worker that owns a dedicated subscription_node and processes all
rcl-mutating tasks (subscribe/unsubscribe/callback-group) on a single
thread. Bounded queue with backpressure (post returns false on full),
deadline-limited run_sync, and shutdown-safe queue drain so pending
run_sync callers always get their promises fulfilled.

Graph-change notifications use the public rclcpp::Node::get_graph_event()
API and poll via a wall timer on the subscription node - no internal
rclcpp APIs, no extra threads beyond the serial worker.

Pre-allocated graph listener slots (16) and deterministic shutdown make
this safe for embedded and (future) automotive deployments.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat: add ErrorInfo type for SOVD provider interfaces

Transport-neutral error descriptor to be used as the error branch of
tl::expected<T, ErrorInfo> by the forthcoming SOVD provider interfaces
(Data, Operation, Fault, DataStream). Handler layer will translate
this into SOVD-compliant GenericError responses.

Refs #375

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): target-filtered per-entity fan-out

Per-entity collection endpoints (/components/{id}/logs, /apps/{id}/data,
/areas/{id}/faults, /functions/{id}/logs, etc.) unconditionally fanned
out req.path to every healthy peer. Peers that do not host the entity
returned 404, the response was flagged as partial with those peers in
failed_peers, even though nothing is broken.

Fan-out is now directed at the peers that actually host or contribute to
the entity:

- AggregationManager tracks a peer_contributors_by_entity_ map alongside
  the existing routing_table_. gateway_node rebuilds both after every
  discovery cycle by walking contributors on the merged entities and
  stripping the 'peer:' prefix.
- get_peer_contributors(id) unions the routing-table owner (routed leaf,
  collision-renamed peer-only entity) with the per-entity contributor
  map (merged Areas/Functions, hierarchical parent Components that were
  stripped from the routing table during classification).
- fan_out_get accepts an optional target_peers list; when supplied, only
  matching healthy peers are queried. Non-contributors never see the
  request, so they cannot appear in failed_peers.
- merge_peer_items extracts the entity id from per-entity paths, asks
  AggregationManager for contributors, and passes the list as the
  target filter. Local-only entities produce an empty list and skip
  fan-out entirely. Global collection endpoints without an entity id
  keep fan-out-to-all behavior.

Covers the common cases: local-only entity (no fan-out), routed leaf
(only the owning peer queried), merged/hierarchical entity (only
contributing peers queried), partial failure isolated to the specific
contributor that failed. Updates aggregation.rst design doc and extends
unit tests for AggregationManager (has_peer_contributors,
get_peer_contributors, empty-entry pruning) and fan-out helpers (owner-
only, contributor-only, partial-only-on-contributor-failure).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(updates): expose phase as x-medkit-phase vendor extension

SOVD UpdateStatus enum collapses prepare-completed and execute-completed
into a single 'completed' value, leaving clients unable to tell whether
the package is ready for Execute or fully installed. Surface the existing
internal UpdatePhase as a vendor extension on /updates/{id}/status so
consumers can distinguish the two without breaking the standard enum.

- Move UpdatePhase into UpdateStatusInfo and emit it as `x-medkit-phase`
- Keep the standard `status` field unchanged (pending|inProgress|completed|failed)
- Document the extension in docs/api/rest.rst with a non-standard callout
- Unit tests for prepared, executed, and freshly-registered (none) serialization

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(tests,ci): stabilize shutdown-race flakes across distros

Integration-test CI has been flaky on Humble and Jazzy with a rotating
victim (demo_calibration_service, demo_brake_actuator,
demo_brake_pressure_sensor, demo_engine_temp_sensor, demo_lidar_sensor,
fault_manager_node) dying during shutdown and failing test_exit_codes.
Prior commits in this area (3adf71b1, 1dc0a7ed, 2f23c098 and others)
added defensive cleanup to individual demo nodes; the crashes kept
moving which was a sign the root cause was not in the nodes. This
change addresses the six distinct bugs that were actually responsible.

1. SIGINT-during-rclcpp-init race in all demo nodes
-----------------------------------------------------
If SIGINT fires between rclcpp::init() and the executor's guard
condition being allocated, rclcpp's default signal handler
invalidates the shared context mid-call; in-flight rcl_service_init /
rcl_guard_condition_init throws RCLError, the exception escapes the
bare demo main() and std::terminate aborts the process with SIGABRT.

Fix: block SIGINT/SIGTERM with pthread_sigmask, let rclcpp::init()
install its handler, construct the node, add it to an explicit
SingleThreadedExecutor (so the guard condition is allocated while
signals are still blocked), then restore the mask. A signal queued in
that window is delivered to a fully-assembled executor and shuts the
node down normally. Applied uniformly to all 10 demo nodes. The
pre-existing std::set_terminate in long_calibration_action.cpp
documents a separate rclcpp_action mid-goal-shutdown race and is
kept.

Local repro on Humble: 3 crashes / 180 iters unpatched vs 0 / 180
patched, in the 50-200 ms post-launch SIGINT window.

2. FastRTPS discovery-teardown use-after-free
-----------------------------------------------
Humble ships FastRTPS 2.6 which has a use-after-free in its
endpoint-discovery-protocol proxy tables on peer disappearance.
When the gateway shuts down cleanly, its "writer leaving" messages
are processed by peer nodes' FastRTPS listener thread which segfaults
in EDP::unpairWriterProxy / PDP::removeWriterProxyData. Backtrace
captured under stress via LD_PRELOAD=libSegFault.so confirms the
crash is in libfastrtps.so, not in our code.

Fix: set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp in the CI test run
environment (both build-and-test matrix covering humble/rolling and
the jazzy-test job). CycloneDDS has a more robust discovery teardown
path.

Local repro: 1 crash / 6 iters with FastRTPS, 0 / 30 with CycloneDDS.
Also install ros-${distro}-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp in the deps step.

3. Unhandled context-invalid throws in fault_manager
------------------------------------------------------
RosbagCapture::get_topic_type, RosbagCapture::resolve_topics, and
SnapshotCapture::get_topic_type invoke node_->get_topic_names_and_types
which throws std::runtime_error when the rcl context is invalidated
mid-call. In RosbagCapture the call is reachable from a discovery
retry timer that fires every 500 ms, and the race window widens under
sanitizer load to the point where the TSan CI job hits it reliably
(SIGABRT / exit -6).

The gateway's cache refresh already catches and logs this
gracefully. Apply the same approach at the three fault_manager call
sites: wrap the rcl call in try/catch and treat invalid-context as
"no topic info available right now" - callers already handle the
empty return (skip subscribe, skip snapshot, retry next tick).

4. TSan-flagged race on RosbagCapture::post_fault_timer_
----------------------------------------------------------
TSan flags a data race on the post_fault_timer_ member
(rclcpp::TimerBase::SharedPtr):

  WRITE  on_fault_confirmed() at rosbag_capture.cpp:208
         (service callback thread)
  READ   post_fault_timer_callback() at rosbag_capture.cpp:656/658
         (main executor thread)

Both paths touch the SharedPtr without synchronisation. Even outside
TSan this is a real use-after-free waiting for the right scheduling.

Fix: introduce std::mutex post_fault_timer_mutex_ and guard every
access (on_fault_confirmed, post_fault_timer_callback, stop). Scope
kept minimal so the executor is not blocked while the service callback
creates the timer.

5. REST server start/stop race in GatewayNode
-----------------------------------------------
GatewayNode::start_rest_server() signalled "server running" on the
worker thread before calling rest_server_->start() (which is where
cpp-httplib's listen() actually binds and enters the accept loop).
For short-lived test fixtures that construct and immediately destroy
a GatewayNode (e.g. the per-test SetUp/TearDown in
test_plugin_notify_integration), the main thread can race ahead and
call stop_rest_server() before the worker has reached listen(). In
that order the stop() request is dropped, listen() subsequently
blocks forever, and the destructor's condition-variable wait hangs
until the 60s test timeout fires.

Fix: drop the server_running_/server_cv_/server_mutex_ machinery and
poll rest_server_->is_running() (which reflects cpp-httplib's actual
accept-loop state). start_rest_server now returns only once the
server is observably ready; stop_rest_server stops and joins directly.
Added RESTServer::is_running() as a passthrough to HttpServerManager.

6. test_cross_ecu_fanout poll accepts pre-discovery responses
---------------------------------------------------------------
test_data_include_peer_topics used `lambda d: d if d.get('items')`
as its readiness predicate. The gateway's /data response contains a
/rosout item as soon as LogManager subscribes, well before demo-node
discovery completes; the poll therefore returned immediately with only
{topic: '/rosout'} and the subsequent assertTrue(has_local) failed.
Tighten the predicate to require both a /powertrain/engine/ item and
a /chassis/brakes/ or /perception/lidar/ item before returning.

Verification
------------
Local stress (Humble container under 16-CPU stress-ng pressure,
LD_PRELOAD=libSegFault.so, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp):
  - 200 iters of test_entity_listing: 0 fails
  -  30 iters of test_triggers_updates: 0 fails
  - fault_manager unit + integration tests: pass
  - test_plugin_notify_integration (Jazzy): 5/5 subtests pass
  - test_cross_ecu_fanout (Jazzy): pass

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(updates): drop redundant id guard in register seed path + CHANGELOG

Callers of UpdateManager::register_update (update_handlers.cpp:108)
already validate that metadata["id"] is a non-empty string before
invoking the manager, so the outer `if (metadata.contains("id") &&
metadata["id"].is_string())` check wrapping the seed block could never
hit its else branch with any in-tree caller. Replace it with a direct
metadata.at("id").get<std::string>() so the precondition is expressed
explicitly and .at() would throw clearly if the contract were ever
broken. The inner `!state_ptr` idempotency check is kept, matching the
pattern in start_prepare / run_prepare.

Add a CHANGELOG.rst entry under Unreleased documenting the observable
contract change: GET /api/v1/updates/{id}/status returns 200 pending
immediately after POST /api/v1/updates, whereas previously 404 was
returned for registered-but-idle packages. 404 is now reserved for
packages that are not registered.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test+docs(updates): cover pending-after-register over HTTP and update rest.rst

Extend test_updates.test.py with an integration test that registers a
package and immediately fetches /updates/{id}/status, asserting a 200
response with status=pending and no progress/error keys - the end-to-end
counterpart to the new UpdateManagerTest.StatusPendingRightAfterRegister
unit test.

Update docs/api/rest.rst to describe the new contract: after a
successful POST /api/v1/updates, GET /api/v1/updates/{id}/status
immediately returns 200 with {"status":"pending"}. 404 is reserved for
packages that are not registered.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(updates): seed Pending state on register so /updates/{id}/status returns 200

Previously UpdateManager::register_update delegated to the backend and
returned without touching states_, so the very next GET /updates/{id}/status
returned 404 with vendor_code x-medkit-update-not-found until the caller
called /prepare. Any UI that gates actions on a non-null status response
(e.g. UpdatesDashboard, which hides Prepare/Execute/Delete buttons when
the status fetch fails) saw newly-registered updates as "Status
unavailable" with no way forward.

Fix: after a successful backend register, seed states_[id] with a
PackageState in phase None and status Pending (idempotent - preserves
any already-seeded state, for symmetry with the defensive pattern used
in the prepare/execute paths).

Unit test StatusPendingRightAfterRegister verifies the new contract:
register returns OK, the immediately following get_status returns a
Pending status with no progress/error. StatusNotFoundForUnknown still
covers the NotFound path for truly unregistered IDs.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(plugins): derive notify integration work_dir from test name + pid

gtest's random_seed() is fixed for the whole process, so every test
case in the fixture reused the same tmp directory. Collisions between
concurrent ctest invocations or between retries of an aborted run
could leak state across test cases. Name the work dir from the current
test-case name plus the pid instead, and wipe it up-front so leftover
state from a prior run is not inherited.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(manifest): expand fragment loader failure coverage

Add cases that lock in the hardened contract:

* BaseAndFragmentDuplicateIdFailsValidation - base declares a
  component id; a fragment that reuses the same id on an app must
  fail the merged validation pass.
* OneBrokenFragmentFailsEntireLoad - one valid sibling plus one
  malformed YAML fragment keeps the prior manifest active (no
  partial application).
* EmptyReservedKeysAreRejected - the raw-YAML presence check
  correctly flags `areas: []`, `metadata: {}`, `scripts: []`,
  `capabilities: {}`, and `lock_overrides: {}`.
* UnknownTopLevelKeyIsIgnoredWithWarning - typos such as `app:`
  do not fail the load, but also do not silently contribute
  entities.
* FragmentOverSizeLimitIsRejected - fragment past 1 MiB hits the
  size cap with a clear error.
* SymlinkEscapingFragmentsDirIsSkipped - a symlink resolving
  outside fragments_dir is skipped with a warning while keeping
  in-tree symlinks usable (the k8s ConfigMap case).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs(plugins): clarify fragment contract and v7 compatibility

Rework the plugin API v7 documentation so the contract matches the
runtime behaviour:

* PLUGIN_API_VERSION is checked with strict equality by the loader, so
  a pre-compiled v6 .so is rejected. Call out source-compatibility
  (v6 source compiles unchanged against v7 headers) vs binary-
  compatibility (not provided - recompilation is required).
* Document the all-or-nothing fragment contract: a single malformed,
  oversized, forbidden, or validation-failing fragment causes the
  whole load / reload to fail, and the previously-loaded manifest
  stays active. Plugins needing independent failure domains should
  use separate fragment directories.
* Document the plugin write contract for fragments_dir: write to a
  tmp file in the same directory, fsync, then rename() atomically
  into place to avoid exposing partial writes to the gateway.
* Reference the 1 MiB size cap and the canonical-path symlink scoping
  now enforced by the fragment loader.

Update CHANGELOG accordingly.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(manifest): cap manifest fragment size at 1 MiB

fragments_dir is user-configurable, so a misconfiguration pointing at a
log file or a symlink to large content could previously feed unbounded
bytes into yaml-cpp, which has no built-in size or depth limits. Reject
any file larger than ManifestParser::kMaxFragmentBytes (1 MiB) in
parse_fragment_file before reading it into memory, with a clear error
naming both the limit and the offending size.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(manifest): inspect raw YAML for forbidden fragment keys

Fragment rejection previously looked at the parsed Manifest struct, so
empty-valued reserved keys (`areas: []`, `metadata: {}`, `scripts: []`,
`capabilities: {}`, `lock_overrides: {}`) were silently accepted because
they produced empty default structs indistinguishable from "not
declared". Switch the check to raw YAML key presence for every
forbidden key (areas, metadata, scripts, capabilities, lock_overrides,
discovery) so the contract matches the docs.

While doing the raw walk, warn on unknown top-level keys that are
neither allowed (apps, components, functions, manifest_version) nor
forbidden. Typos such as `app:` vs `apps:` no longer silently produce
empty fragments - the user gets a clear log line naming the bad key.

Also resolve each directory entry through std::filesystem::canonical
and skip any path whose real location is not a descendant of the
configured fragments_dir. Symlinks are still followed (k8s ConfigMap
mounts rely on that) but `evil.yaml -> /etc/shadow` style escapes are
rejected with a warning.

Tighten the apply_fragments docstring to match the actual contract:
duplicate IDs are caught by ManifestValidator::validate() over the
merged manifest, not by apply_fragments itself.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(manifest): anchor manifest_version detection to column 0

parse_fragment_file scans the raw YAML source to decide whether a
fragment already declares `manifest_version:` before it injects a
synthetic `"1.0"`. The scanner matched the token at any indentation,
so a nested sub-map key of the same name (e.g. inside `ros_binding:`
or a plugin's custom metadata block) was treated as a manifest-level
declaration, injection was skipped, and `parse_string` then rejected
the fragment with "Missing required field: manifest_version".

Require the match at column 0 - only an un-indented line counts as a
top-level key for the yaml dialect we accept. A regression test
exercises the nested-key case so the tolerance does not come back.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(plugins): log reload failure in notify_entities_changed

handle_entity_change_notification ignored the bool return of
ManifestManager::reload_manifest(). A plugin that dropped a malformed
fragment and then notified would see a successful-looking
RCLCPP_INFO("Plugin entity-change notification: ...") and a normal
refresh, while the underlying reload had silently failed and the
previous manifest was still in use. Emit RCLCPP_WARN pointing at
ManifestManager::get_validation_result() so operators and plugins can
diagnose the rejection.

The accompanying test pins the observable contract: after notifying
with a forbidden-field fragment the base manifest is preserved AND the
validation result surfaces the FRAGMENT_FORBIDDEN_FIELD error.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(plugins): guard notify_entities_changed against introspect reentrancy

refresh_cache() invokes provider->introspect() on every loaded plugin.
A v7 plugin can legitimately call PluginContext::notify_entities_changed
from inside its own introspect callback (e.g., after introspect
discovers a new entity on disk). The recursive refresh mutex happily
lets that path re-enter, producing an unbounded notify -> reload ->
refresh -> introspect -> notify loop until stack exhaustion.

Track a per-thread "inside refresh pass" flag:
  * handle_entity_change_notification short-circuits with a warning
    when the flag is already set on the caller's thread;
  * both handle_entity_change_notification and refresh_cache set the
    flag for the duration of their own pass via RAII guards.

The reference header comment is also extended to forbid the reentry
pattern (see docs(plugins) commit). A new integration test exercises
the guard via a dedicated test hook; adding the full plugin harness
just to exercise this path would be disproportionate.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs(plugins): align notify_entities_changed thread-safety contract

The v7 header promised non-blocking / queue-based semantics that the
reference implementation does not deliver. Rewrite the Thread safety
section to describe the actual synchronous, refresh-mutex-serialized
behavior and call out the two patterns that were easy to get wrong:
holding a plugin-owned mutex across the call (deadlock) and calling
notify from within an IntrospectionProvider::introspect() callback
(now explicitly no-op + warn in the reference gateway).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(plugins): reserve unique port in notify integration test

The test used `server.enabled:=false` as if it were a real parameter
override, but GatewayNode does not declare `server.enabled`. rclcpp
silently dropped the override, so the test started its REST server on
the default port 8080 - colliding with every other parallel gtest that
spins up a GatewayNode. Switch to the project's standard port-isolation
pattern: reserve a free loopback port with reserve_local_port() and
pass it via server.port / server.host (matches test_discovery_handlers,
test_handler_context, test_gateway_node).

data.message: style: reformat RCLCPP_INFO call in discovery_manager

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message: style: apply clang-format 18 to plugin notify + fragment files

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(review): address Copilot findings on PR #377

* Serialize refresh_cache() with a recursive mutex covering both the
  refresh timer callback and the plugin notify_entities_changed path
  (including the preceding reload_manifest() step). Fixes a real data
  race where HybridDiscoveryStrategy::refresh() - which assumes
  single-threaded invocation - could run concurrently on the executor
  thread and a plugin thread.
* Update gateway_node.hpp and plugin_context.cpp comments to describe
  the actual synchronous, refresh-mutex-serialized call semantics
  instead of the imagined queuing / cache-mutex story.
* Reject more forbidden top-level fields in manifest fragments:
  metadata.description, metadata.created_at (so the whole metadata
  block is off-limits, not just name/version) and the top-level
  discovery block (detected by re-parsing the YAML because
  ManifestConfig defaults are indistinguishable from absence).
  Manifest manager, parser, design doc and changelog docstrings now
  describe the real behavior - forbidden fields are validation
  errors, not warnings. Added three gtest cases covering the new
  rejections.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test+docs(plugins): integration test, design doc, CHANGELOG entry

Integration test (test/test_plugin_notify_integration.cpp) drives a
real GatewayNode through the full plugin lifecycle:
- HYBRID discovery with a tiny base manifest on disk
- fragments_dir pointing at a tmp directory
- real PluginContext from make_gateway_plugin_context
Asserts that:
- a fragment dropped after startup + notify makes the new app visible
- a fragment removed after startup + notify makes the app disappear
- notify with no fragments is a safe no-op and does not drop the
  base-manifest entities

Along the way, wire handle_entity_change_notification to reload the
manifest source before running refresh_cache - without that,
fragments added since the last load stay invisible to the pipeline.

design/plugin_entity_notifications.rst walks through the lifecycle
and documents the fragment merge rules.

CHANGELOG.rst gains an Unreleased section describing the plugin API
v7 bump and the new discovery.manifest.fragments_dir parameter.

refs #376

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(manifest): merge fragment files from a configured directory

Adds a discovery.manifest.fragments_dir gateway parameter. When set, the
ManifestManager scans that directory on every load / reload and merges
apps, components, and functions from each `*.yaml` / `*.yml` file on top
of the base manifest before the validator runs. This lets plugins that
deploy new entities at runtime drop a manifest chunk alongside their
deployed files without editing the base manifest, and remove it on
rollback.

Merge rules (enforced in ManifestManager::apply_fragments):
- fragments contribute only apps, components, functions
- fragments may not declare areas, metadata, scripts, capabilities, or
  lock_overrides; each forbidden field is reported as a
  FRAGMENT_FORBIDDEN_FIELD validation error
- fragment files are applied in alphabetical order, making duplicate-id
  errors deterministic
- a missing fragments directory is treated as "no fragments", not an
  error (plugins can create the directory lazily on first install)

ManifestParser gains parse_fragment_file, which injects the synthetic
`manifest_version: "1.0"` header fragments are not required to declare.

Tests cover: no fragments, missing dir, single merge, deterministic
order with multiple files, non-yaml file skipped, forbidden `areas`
field, duplicate ids across fragments, reload picks up added and
removed files, set/get accessor round-trip.

refs #376

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(plugins): notify_entities_changed lifecycle hook and API v7

Plugins that mutate the entity surface at runtime (deploying a new node
under a manifest fragment, removing a previously-deployed app, renaming
a component) had no way to tell the gateway "my entities changed, refresh
your tree". Callers were left racing the runtime-discovery polling tick
or restarting the gateway.

This adds a dedicated plugin hook:

  virtual void PluginContext::notify_entities_changed(
      const EntityChangeScope& scope);

The default implementation is a no-op so plugins built against plugin API
v6 continue to load unchanged. Bump PLUGIN_API_VERSION from 6 to 7.

EntityChangeScope is a small hint struct with optional area_id and
component_id fields plus a full_refresh() convenience. The current gateway
implementation always does a full refresh_cache() pass on notification -
the scope is accepted and logged for forward compatibility with a future
scoped-refresh optimization.

Part 1 of a larger piece tracked in issue #376; the companion manifest
fragments directory support lands in a follow-up change.

refs #376

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(review): second Copilot round - aggregation flag semantics + missing RESOURCE_LOCK

Two additional valid findings on top of 73d1433b:

- docs/api/rest.rst described capabilities.aggregation as "true when
  the gateway has one or more aggregation peers configured", but the
  implementation gates it on AggregationManager presence (i.e. the
  subsystem is enabled regardless of peer count). A gateway with
  aggregation.enabled=true and zero peers still sets the flag to true
  and still emits peers/warnings on /health. Rephrase the docs so the
  semantics match the code and callers understand that peers may be
  empty while the flag is still true.
- test_cross_ecu_fanout also calls get_test_domain_id(1) and therefore
  claims domain 230, same as test_peer_aggregation. The CTest
  RESOURCE_LOCK medkit_secondary_dds_domains that 73d1433b added only
  covered the two multi-gateway tests I remembered; add
  test_cross_ecu_fanout to the same lock so it is serialised against
  the rest and cannot race for the shared domain under parallel CTest
  runs. Comment updated to remind future additions to list every test
  that calls get_test_domain_id with a non-zero offset here.

Part of PR #374.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(review): address Copilot review findings on PR #374

Seven inline review comments from Copilot, all valid after verifying
against the actual diff:

- area.hpp relied on sorted_contributors() (defined in common.hpp) from
  its inline to_json() without including the header. component.hpp and
  function.hpp were already fine; add the include to area.hpp so every
  public model header is self-contained regardless of include order.
- get_test_domain_id() previously collapsed every non-zero offset into
  a single derived secondary domain via (base - 140) % 3, so using
  offsets 2 and 3 in the daisy-chain test produced the SAME DDS domain
  for peer_b and peer_c (the earlier docstring was also wrong about
  this). Return 229 + offset so offsets 1..3 map one-to-one to
  domains 230..232, and reject offsets outside that range with a clear
  ValueError - the DDS maximum is 232 so silently exceeding it must
  fail loudly. Pair this with a CTest RESOURCE_LOCK on
  test_peer_aggregation and test_daisy_chain_aggregation so the two
  multi-gateway tests never share a secondary domain in parallel runs.
- test_leaf_component_detail_contributors_single_peer had a leading
  comment that claimed the assertion was about contributors equalling
  ["peer:peer_b"] while the actual check was for "local" first. Rewrite
  the docstring so it matches the forwarded-response semantics the test
  actually pins (peer_b's own view serialised verbatim by the primary).
- docs/api/warning_codes.rst did not exist, yet two header/source
  comments pointed at it. Add the page with the stable warning-code
  table (currently just leaf_id_collision) plus remediation guidance,
  link it from the API reference index, and point warning_codes.hpp +
  schema_builder.cpp at a now-valid canonical location.
- docs/api/rest.rst did not document the new /health.warnings array or
  the capabilities.aggregation flag. Add both: root-endpoint capability
  gets an example and a one-paragraph description; /health grows an
  aggregation-aware example response showing peers and warnings with a
  realistic leaf_id_collision payload.

Tests: 2015 unit + integration still green locally; Sphinx docs build
with -W warnings-as-errors stays clean.

Part of PR #374.

data.author: Bartosz Burda

feat(openapi): document x-medkit.contributors on the EntityDetail schema

declared at all, which meant generated clients silently dropped the

contributors property (typed array of strings, with a description
covering the "local" vs "peer:<name>" semantics and the stable sort
order). additionalProperties remains true so that existing x-medkit
fields not yet typed at the schema level (entityType, namespace,
source, etc.) continue to round-trip cleanly.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): consistent x-medkit.contributors emission + deterministic output

Review follow-ups for PR #374 addressing correctness and determinism
gaps found in deep-review:

- Previously x-medkit.contributors was emitted only on GET /components/{id}
  because the Component detail handler builds x-medkit manually via the
  XMedkit builder. Area/App/Function detail handlers silently dropped the
  field despite the models carrying it. Introduce XMedkit::contributors()
  helper and call it from all four detail handlers so list and detail
  endpoints expose provenance consistently.

- Classification output is now deterministic: leaf_warnings are sorted by
  entity_id, each warning's peer_names list is sorted alphabetically,
  and per-peer claim iteration is driven by a sorted copy of the
  unordered_set. Operator logs and /health.warnings no longer flap
  between runs or after hashmap rehashes.

- Contributors are presented in stable order ("local" first when present,
  then peer:<name> entries alphabetically) via a sorted_contributors()
  helper in discovery/models/common.hpp. Called from every entity
  to_json() and from XMedkit::contributors(), so list and detail
  responses agree regardless of how peers were merged.

- Introduce warning_codes.hpp with WARN_LEAF_ID_COLLISION constant
  mirroring the error_codes.hpp pattern. Inline string literal in
  health_handlers.cpp replaced with the constant.

- Leaf-collision warning message now names the colliding peers and
  includes a concrete remediation hint (rename on one side, or model
  as hierarchical parent) instead of only describing the symptom.

- Add aggregation capability flag to handle_root so clients can
  feature-detect that /health.warnings and x-medkit.contributors may
  be present. /health.warnings is always an array when aggregation
  is enabled (empty when no anomalies), so clients avoid tri-state
  absent/empty/populated branching.

- OpenAPI health_schema() now declares top-level peers and warnings
  fields (with structured warning object schema for code/message/
  entity_ids/peer_names). Previously these were emitted but absent
  from the spec - breaking client generators.

Tests: 1980 unit + daisy-chain integration still green. Deeper
integration coverage (leaf collision path, capability assertion,
contributors on non-Component entities) follows in a separate commit.

Part of PR #374.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
test(aggregation): integration test for daisy-chain hierarchical aggregation

Launch three gateways in separate DDS domains (primary -> peer_B ->
peer_C), each with a manifest that declares a shared hierarchical
parent 'robot-x' plus a single leaf ECU sub-component (ecu-a / ecu-b /
ecu-c). Manifests are written to tmp files at import time so launch
descriptions reference stable paths.

Validates end-to-end:
- Primary sees all three ECU sub-components under robot-x, including
  ecu-c which arrives via transitive aggregation through peer_B.
- GET /components/robot-x returns a locally-served response with
  x-medkit.contributors listing "local" and "peer:peer_b" (each hop
  surfaces only its direct upstream; peer_c's contribution is opaque
  to the primary).
- GET /components/ecu-b succeeds via 1-hop forwarding to peer_B.
- GET /components/ecu-c succeeds via 2-hop forwarding primary ->
  peer_B -> peer_C.
- GET /health on primary returns a peers list plus an empty warnings
  array (no leaf-id collisions in this topology).

Also surfaces Component contributors in the detail handler's x-medkit
block, which was missing because handle_get_component builds its
x-medkit via XMedkit rather than the Component::to_json() path used by
list/reference endpoints.

Part of PR #374.
