data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(aggregation): expose merge provenance via x-medkit.contributors

Single-string source cannot express that an entity was contributed by
both the local gateway and one or more peers. Add a contributors field
on Area, Component, App, and Function models, serialised in each
entity's x-medkit block (only when non-empty, so the field is a pure
additive extension for existing clients). Single-origin entities get a
one-element list for consistency.

Population:
- AggregationManager seeds every local entity with ["local"] before the
  per-peer merge loop.
- EntityMerger appends "peer:<name>" on collisions (Areas, Components,
  Functions) and on remote-only additions; deduplication protects
  against repeated merges with the same peer.
- App collision-prefixed entities receive only the peer contributor
  since the prefixed ID is a distinct entity.

Daisy-chain note: each hop surfaces only its direct upstream
("peer:<name>") - a primary aggregating peer_B sees peer_B's entities
as contributed by peer_B regardless of whether peer_B itself merged
them from peer_C. This is intentional and can be extended later.

Part of PR #374.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(health): expose aggregation leaf-collision warnings via /health.warnings

When more than one peer announces the same leaf Component ID,
AggregationManager stores the collision as a structured warning. The
/health endpoint now surfaces these via a top-level warnings array
(x-medkit extension on our own endpoint, not SOVD core). Empty array
when no warnings are active. Operators can pick up deployment anomalies
without tailing logs; routing still falls back to last-writer-wins.

Each warning carries a machine-readable code, human message, the
affected entity_ids (currently a single-element array for forward
compatibility), and the full list of claiming peer_names.

Part of PR #374.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(aggregation): wire classify_component_routing into AggregationManager

Track per-peer Component IDs during fetch_and_merge_peer_entities and
run classify_component_routing once the merged Component set is final.
Hierarchical-parent routing entries are stripped (served locally with
the merged view, like Areas/Functions); leaves keep routing to their
peer. Multi-peer leaf collisions surface as RCLCPP_WARN log entries
listing every claiming peer, and the structured warnings are returned
on MergedPeerResult.leaf_warnings for downstream consumers (e.g. the
upcoming /health.warnings field).

Existing unit (1976) and peer-aggregation integration (82) suites pass
unchanged - the no-collision and apps-only paths still match the prior
behaviour because classify_component_routing is a no-op for those.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(aggregation): GREEN classify_component_routing free function

Introduce a pure free function that takes the fully-merged Component
vector plus per-peer Component claims and returns a routing table with
hierarchical parents removed plus a list of multi-peer leaf-collision
warnings. Hierarchical parent = any Component referenced as
parent_component_id by another Component in the set. Leaves stay routed
to their peer (last-writer-wins for routing on collision; warning
enumerates every claiming peer).

Fixes the 6 red tests added in the previous commit.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
docs(aggregation): document ECU ownership on collision-merged components

Update the merge-rules summary, the merge-logic PlantUML diagram, and
the routing-table description to reflect that a Component ID
identifies a single physical ECU. On collision the peer is always the
authoritative owner, so every request for the merged Component -
including the detail endpoint and all sub-resources - is forwarded to
that peer. The primary's local view is limited to aggregating the
Component's presence in discovery listings.

Replace the test that asserted merged Components stay out of the
routing table (which encoded the prior incorrect "shared ownership"
model) with one that asserts the opposite: merged Components must
route to the peer that owns the ECU's runtime state. Add a dedicated

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): add routing entry for collision-merged peer components

When a peer component collides with a local one (e.g. hybrid mode
creates a synthetic component that matches a peer's real component),
the merged entity was not added to the routing table. This caused
sub-resource requests (logs, hosts, data) to be handled locally
instead of forwarded to the peer, returning empty results.

Add routing_table_[merged.id] = peer_name_ in the collision branch
of merge_components so that validate_entity_for_route forwards
requests to the owning peer.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): write_data() use 3-arg write_value with data_type_hint + error mapping

Bug fix from review:
- write_data() was calling 2-arg write_value(node_id, value) (bool
  return) instead of 3-arg write_value(node_id, value, data_type_hint)
  (tl::expected return). This meant writes through standard SOVD
  PUT /data/{name} missed the type hint optimization AND collapsed all
  errors to generic 502.
- Now matches handle_plc_operations() and execute_operation() which
  correctly pass entry->data_type and map WriteError codes to
  appropriate HTTP status.

Also: remove redundant `using namespace ros2_medkit_gateway;` inside
the already-open `namespace ros2_medkit_gateway { }` block.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): remove alarm integration assertions, keep SOVD data test

The alarm trigger/clear assertions fail because the OpenPLC tank demo's
IEC 61131-3 program continuously recalculates TankLevel from pump/drain
physics. External writes to TankLevel via OPC-UA are overridden on the
next PLC cycle (100ms), so we cannot force the value below the alarm
threshold to trigger PLC_LOW_LEVEL.

Remove the alarm assertions (they need a PLC program that cooperates
with external writes, or a longer simulation-based approach). Keep the
SOVD /data endpoint assertions which prove DataProvider integration
end-to-end. Integration total: 18 assertions (16 original + 2 SOVD).

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): use polling loop for alarm integration test instead of fixed sleep

The alarm trigger test was flaky in CI because the 3s fixed sleep was
not enough for the full pipeline: PLC write -> poller read -> threshold
cross -> alarm callback -> ROS 2 service -> fault_manager DB -> HTTP
response. Replace with a 15-iteration polling loop (1s per iteration)
that exits as soon as the fault appears/clears.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): richer write errors, YAML validation, poll_interval clamp, backoff

Write error types (#23, #24):
- Change write_value return from bool to tl::expected<void, WriteErrorInfo>
  with specific error codes: NotConnected, TypeMismatch, AccessDenied,
  NodeNotFound, TransportError
- Add data_type_hint parameter to skip the readValue type-probe round-trip
  when the caller knows the expected type from NodeMap; halves mutex hold
  time on writes
- Callers (vendor route handlers + DataProvider::write_data +
  OperationProvider::execute_operation) map WriteError codes to
  appropriate HTTP status (400 for type mismatch, 403 for access denied,
  502 for transport errors) instead of generic 502 for all failures

YAML validation (#19):
- Validate required fields (node_id, entity_id, data_name) per entry;
  skip with RCLCPP_WARN if missing
- Validate data_type is one of bool/int/float/string; default to float
  with warning if unknown
- Detect duplicate node_id entries; first wins, subsequent skipped with
  warning
- Cap node count at 10000 to prevent DDS resource exhaustion from
  oversized configs
- Replace all std::cerr output with RCLCPP_WARN/RCLCPP_ERROR for
  structured logging

Poll interval clamp (#20):
- Clamp poll_interval_ms to [100, 60000] in configure() so sub-100ms
  values no longer cause a CPU spin even without the condition_variable
  fix from the previous commit

Exponential backoff on reconnect (#28):
- Double the reconnect wait on each failed attempt, capped at 60s
- Reset to configured interval on successful reconnect
- Prevents network and log saturation when PLC is down for extended
  periods

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): explicit tl::expected construction for Humble compiler compat

Humble's older tl::expected header considers the implicit conversion
from nlohmann::json to tl::expected<json, ErrorInfo> ambiguous when
both the value type and the error type have user-defined constructors.
Wrap all direct json returns from DataProvider, OperationProvider and
FaultProvider methods in explicit tl::expected<json, XxxErrorInfo>{...}
construction. Jazzy and Rolling accept both forms; Humble requires the
explicit one.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
feat(opcua): implement DataProvider + OperationProvider + FaultProvider; harden plugin

Address all critical and important findings from maintainer review:

Provider migration (#11 critical):
- Implement DataProvider (list_data, read_data, write_data) so standard
  SOVD GET/PUT /{type}/{id}/data endpoints work for PLC entities
- Implement OperationProvider (list_operations, execute_operation) for
  POST /{type}/{id}/operations/{name}
- Implement FaultProvider (list_faults, get_fault, clear_fault) for

- Keep all vendor x-plc-* routes for backward compat + rich PLC data
- MCP tools (sovd_read_data etc.), Web UI, fleet gateway now work on

Shutdown guard (#13 important):
- Add std::atomic<bool> shutdown_requested_ with exchange(true) pattern
- Destructor calls shutdown() (was = default)
- Callbacks (publish_values, on_alarm_change) check flag before work
- All 4 route handlers + 8 provider methods return 503 when shutdown

Null checks (#14 important):
- All route handlers and provider methods check ctx_ and poller_ at
  entry, returning 503 ERR_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE if uninitialized

Condition variable sleep (#15 important):
- Replace integer-division sleep loops in opcua_poller with
  std::condition_variable::wait_for so stop() wakes the thread
  immediately and sub-100ms intervals no longer cause CPU spin
- Replace assert(!running_) in set_poll_callback with std::logic_error

Small fixes (#21, #22, #25, #26):
- SecurityPolicy=None warning now includes endpoint URL
- FetchContent GIT_TAG pinned to full SHA (122ea4c8) instead of

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): deterministic entity ordering in NodeMap::build_entity_defs

``build_entity_defs`` used a ``std::unordered_map<string, PlcEntityDef>``
to group entries by entity_id and then iterated it to populate
``entity_defs_``. ``unordered_map`` iteration order is
implementation-defined and can vary across runs, compiler versions and
bucket layouts, so downstream consumers of ``IntrospectionResult`` saw
noisy, unstable entity ordering.

Sort ``entity_defs_`` by id after the grouping pass. Small, cheap, and
removes a whole class of diff noise / flaky-test risk.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): register plc capabilities per entity, not type-level

Previously ``set_context()`` registered ``x-plc-data`` and
``x-plc-operations`` as type-level APP capabilities and ``x-plc-status``
as a type-level COMPONENT capability. That made every app and every
component in the shared SOVD entity tree advertise the plc-* endpoints
in its capability discovery response - including ROS 2 entities served
by other plugins (e.g. graph_provider apps) that have no PLC backing at
all. Clients would see the capabilities, call the endpoints and get
404s because ``NodeMap::entries_for_entity`` returned empty for those
non-PLC entities. Web UIs that trust capability discovery would show
PLC controls on ROS 2 nodes that do not have them.

Drop the three type-level ``register_capability`` calls and replace
them with per-entity ``register_entity_capability`` calls inside
``introspect()``:

- ``x-plc-status`` registered on the single PLC runtime component
- ``x-plc-data`` registered on every PLC-backed app
- ``x-plc-operations`` registered only on PLC apps that have writable
  nodes (as before, now without the duplicate type-level entry)

No runtime behavior change for PLC entities (the routes and handlers
are unchanged). ROS 2 entities no longer advertise capabilities they
cannot serve.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): mark connection as dropped on read_values / write_value failures

``OpcuaClient::read_value`` already caught ``BadConnectionClosed``,
``BadSecureChannelClosed`` and ``BadNotConnected`` status codes and
flipped ``impl_->connected`` to false so ``OpcuaPoller::poll_loop``
would pick up the drop on the next iteration and trigger a reconnect.
The batch ``read_values`` path and the ``write_value`` path caught
``BadStatus`` but never updated the flag, leaving the plugin in a
"connected=true but everything fails" zombie state until something
else happened to hit the single-node read path.

Extract the check into a small ``maybe_mark_disconnected`` helper in an
anonymous namespace and call it from all three catch blocks. The
poller's existing reconnect logic keys off ``is_connected()`` so no
other changes are needed - once the flag is flipped the next cycle will
reconnect.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(opcua): use yaml_cpp_vendor + medkit_find_yaml_cpp for multi-distro compat

Replace the direct ``find_package(yaml-cpp REQUIRED)`` + bare
``yaml-cpp`` link with the medkit-standard ``yaml_cpp_vendor`` dependency
and the ``medkit_find_yaml_cpp()`` helper from ``ROS2MedkitCompat.cmake``.

Rest of medkit (gateway, serialization, fault_manager) already uses this
pattern because Humble's native apt yaml-cpp does not consistently export
a CMake target. Plugin was the odd one out.

Also drop the three redundant ``target_compile_options(... -Wno-conversion)``
calls on the plugin and test targets. With ``open62541pp``'s interface
include directories marked as SYSTEM via
``INTERFACE_SYSTEM_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES``, GCC already suppresses the
``-Wconversion`` / ``-Wsign-conversion`` warnings from third-party
headers. A clean rebuild with the flags removed produces zero warnings,
so the flags were not protecting anything - they were just silently
disabling a safety net for our own future code.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
docs(opcua): reflect full node ID support in design doc

After the previous commit the plugin can address OPC-UA nodes using all
four identifier types defined by OPC 10000-6 section 5.3.1.10 (i, s, g,
b), which means the same binary works against any compliant OPC-UA
server without a code change. Only the node map YAML changes per vendor.

Update design/index.rst accordingly:

- Add a new `Supported PLC servers` section calling out that Siemens
  S7-1500, Beckhoff TwinCAT 3, Allen-Bradley via Kepware, KUKA KR C5 and
  OpenPLC all work, with a pointer to the example YAML.
- Enumerate the real remaining gaps that are still vendor/feature
  limitations: complex OPC-UA types (structures, arrays, enums), vendor
  information models (Euromap, Siemens DI, PA-DIM) and native AlarmCondition
  events.
- Drop the vague "Vendor-specific extensions for common PLC brands"
  future-work bullet - it conflated node addressing (now covered) with
  complex types and information models (still missing and now called out
  explicitly).
- Add complex types and AlarmCondition ingestion to Future work as
  concrete follow-up targets.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
feat(opcua): support all four OPC-UA node ID identifier types

Extend NodeMap::parse_node_id to handle the full OPC 10000-6 section
5.3.1.10 node ID string format:

    [ns=<ns-index>;]i=<uint32>     numeric   (OpenPLC, compact servers)
    [ns=<ns-index>;]s=<string>     string    (Siemens DB, Beckhoff tags)
    [ns=<ns-index>;]g=<guid>       GUID      (Microsoft-style UUID)
    [ns=<ns-index>;]b=<base64>     opaque    (binary ByteString)

Previously the parser only supported numeric (i=) and string (s=)
identifiers, which was enough for the OpenPLC tank demo but excluded
most real industrial PLC servers. With this change integrators can
point `node_id:` at any Siemens S7 DB address, Beckhoff TwinCAT POU
path, Allen-Bradley tag, KUKA KRC state variable, or legacy system
using GUID/opaque identifiers - without any plugin code change.

Parser behavior:

- `ns=` prefix is optional; missing namespace defaults to 0 (standard
  OPC-UA namespace).
- GUID identifiers are parsed via a small hex parser that accepts both
  the bare `XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX` form and the
  Microsoft registry form with curly braces `{...}`.
- Opaque ByteString identifiers are parsed via
  `opcua::ByteString::fromBase64` from open62541pp.
- String identifiers are taken verbatim after the `s=` prefix so they
  can contain semicolons, quotes, dots, and other punctuation that
  Siemens DB addresses rely on.
- Malformed inputs return a default-constructed `opcua::NodeId` which
  the runtime treats as unresolvable.

`parse_node_id` is now public so it can be unit-tested directly and
reused by the upcoming browse CLI (#368).

Tests: 12 new gtest cases in test_node_map.cpp covering numeric
with/without namespace, Siemens-style string, Beckhoff-style string,
string with embedded semicolons, GUID with and without curly braces,
opaque base64, and malformed inputs.

Documentation: tank_demo_nodes.yaml now carries a comment block
explaining the node ID format and showing ready-to-copy examples for
OpenPLC (this demo), Siemens S7-1500 TIA Portal, Beckhoff TwinCAT 3,
Allen-Bradley via Kepware, KUKA KR C5, GUID identifiers, and opaque
ByteString identifiers.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
ci(opcua): fix rosdep keys and drop redundant packages-skip

Two follow-up fixes to the unit-tests job added in the previous commit:

1. Stop skipping `ament_cmake_clang_format` and `test_msgs` in the
   rosdep install call. These are real build-time test dependencies
   pulled in transitively by `ros2_medkit_serialization` and the
   gateway, and skipping them causes `find_package(ament_cmake_clang_format REQUIRED)`
   at configure time of those upstream packages to fail. `nav2_msgs`
   is kept in the skip list because it is declared by `vda5050_agent`
   (which we do not build here) and is not available on all distros.

2. Drop `--packages-skip vda5050_agent ros2_medkit_vda5050_msgs` from
   the colcon build invocation. `--packages-up-to ros2_medkit_opcua`
   already walks the dependency graph starting at the plugin and will
   naturally exclude anything that is not a dependency, so the
   explicit skip is redundant.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
ci: skip ros2_medkit_opcua in base matrix, cover it via opcua-plugin.yml

Pin ros2_medkit_opcua out of the base ci.yml build + test commands
with `--packages-skip`. The plugin pulls open62541pp via FetchContent
which adds noticeable time to every matrix run for packages that are
completely unrelated to the plugin.

Multi-distro (Humble + Jazzy + Rolling) unit test coverage is kept by
adding a new `unit-tests` job to the existing `opcua-plugin.yml`
workflow, which is already guarded by a path filter so it only runs
when the plugin, its upstream plugin API, or ros2_medkit_msgs change.
The integration job (Docker + OpenPLC) runs alongside on the same
trigger.

Effect:

- PRs that do not touch the plugin pay zero extra cost (base ci.yml
  is unchanged for all other packages, and opcua-plugin.yml does not
  run)
- PRs that touch the plugin run both the multi-distro unit test
  matrix and the Docker integration suite
- The nightly cron on opcua-plugin.yml serves as a safety net for
  transitive breakage that slips past path filters

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
ci: add OPC-UA plugin integration workflow

New workflow `opcua-plugin.yml` that runs the Docker-based
integration suite for `ros2_medkit_opcua`: builds an OpenPLC tank
demo container, starts it alongside the gateway image with the
plugin loaded, waits for entity discovery and live PLC data, then
runs the 16-assertion `run_integration_tests.sh` script.

Triggers only on changes that could affect plugin behavior:

- `src/ros2_medkit_plugins/ros2_medkit_opcua/**`
- `src/ros2_medkit_gateway/include/ros2_medkit_gateway/plugins/**`
- `src/ros2_medkit_gateway/include/ros2_medkit_gateway/providers/**`
- `src/ros2_medkit_gateway/include/ros2_medkit_gateway/http/error_codes.hpp`
- `src/ros2_medkit_msgs/**`
- `.github/workflows/opcua-plugin.yml` itself

Unrelated PRs do not pay the ~5 minute open62541pp build cost
because of the path filter. Including the gateway plugin API
headers in the trigger paths prevents silent breakage when the
plugin base class evolves.

A nightly cron (04:00 UTC) provides a safety net against breaks
that slip past the path filter (for example, transitive changes
via rosdep keys or base image updates). The workflow also dumps
gateway and OpenPLC logs on failure to make debugging easier.

The base `ci.yml` continues to build and test `ros2_medkit_opcua`
as part of its Humble / Jazzy / Rolling matrix via the normal
colcon flow; this new workflow is additive, only covering the
end-to-end integration tier that needs Docker containers.

Refs #364

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
feat(plugins): add ros2_medkit_opcua plugin package

Introduce a new colcon package `ros2_medkit_opcua` under
`src/ros2_medkit_plugins/` that bridges OPC-UA capable PLCs
(OpenPLC, Siemens S7, Beckhoff, Allen-Bradley, etc.) into the
SOVD entity tree.

The plugin implements `GatewayPlugin` + `IntrospectionProvider`
against the current `get_routes()` plugin API and ships:

- OpcuaPlugin - lifecycle, REST routes, introspection, fault bridge
- OpcuaClient - open62541pp wrapper: connect, type-aware read/write
- OpcuaPoller - background poll or OPC-UA subscription with
  threshold-based alarm detection
- NodeMap - YAML-driven PLC tag to SOVD entity mapping with
  range validation

Vendor REST endpoints registered via get_routes:
  GET  /apps/{id}/x-plc-data          - all PLC values for an entity
  GET  /apps/{id}/x-plc-data/{node}   - single value
  POST /apps/{id}/x-plc-operations/{op} - write with type + range check
  GET  /components/{id}/x-plc-status  - connection state and metrics

PLC alarms are routed to SOVD faults via
`/fault_manager/report_fault` and `/fault_manager/clear_fault`.
Numeric PLC values are also published as `std_msgs/Float32` topics
(one publisher per node) so ROS 2 consumers can plot them without
speaking OPC-UA.

Build:
- Follows the `ros2_medkit_graph_provider` template for CMake
  structure: ROS2MedkitCompat, ROS2MedkitCcache, ROS2MedkitSanitizers,
  ROS2MedkitWarnings, ROS2MedkitTestDomain.
- `open62541pp` v0.16.0 (MPLv2, linked as unmodified library) is
  pulled via FetchContent with its GIT_TAG pinned. Directory-level
  COMPILE_OPTIONS are cleared around FetchContent_MakeAvailable so
  the strict warning flags from ROS2MedkitWarnings do not fire on
  upstream C sources. Interface include directories are marked as
  SYSTEM on the open62541pp target so consumers do not inherit
  `-Wsign-conversion`/`-Wconversion` noise from the headers.

Tests:
- gtest unit tests for NodeMap YAML parsing and OpcuaClient config
  validation (test_node_map, test_opcua_client).
- Docker-based integration suite under `docker/` - OpenPLC container
  running an IEC 61131-3 tank demo (`tank_demo.st`) plus 16 assertions
  covering entity discovery, PLC connection, live data, pump/valve
  writes and error handling. Used by the dedicated CI workflow added
  in a follow-up commit.

Demo assets:
- `config/tank_demo_nodes.yaml` - example node map
- `docker/openplc/` - OpenPLC container with `tank_demo.st` ST program
- `docker/scripts/` - start/stop/test integration scripts shared
  between local development and CI

Documentation: README.md, CHANGELOG.rst (0.4.0 - Forthcoming),
design/index.rst covering architecture, poll vs subscription
trade-off, alarm mapping, and security limitations.

Refs #364

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: skip fan-out when no healthy peers to protect httplib thread pool

merge_peer_items now checks healthy_peer_count() before initiating
fan-out. With fan-out on all per-entity collection endpoints, concurrent
requests during a peer outage could block handler threads for up to
timeout_ms each, exhausting httplib's thread pool. The early return
ensures requests complete immediately once health checks detect the
peer is down.

Also documents the thread-pool interaction and timeout implications
in the aggregation design doc.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): support HAL+JSON object-form _links and add edge case tests

parse_app() now handles the HAL+JSON object form for _links entries
({"href": "..."}) in addition to bare strings, so strictly-compliant

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(tests): lock callback_mutex_ in subscription callbacks of brake_actuator and light_controller

Commit 89eaac6 added callback_mutex_ to timer callbacks across all demo
nodes but missed the subscription callbacks in brake_actuator and
light_controller. Their command_callback wrote to shared state
(target_pressure_, light_on_) outside the mutex, and the destructor
reset cmd_sub_ before acquiring the lock - leaving a window where a
command message arriving during shutdown could race with teardown and
produce a SIGSEGV (humble CI, test_scenario_discovery_hybrid
test_exit_codes, exit code -11).

Apply the full pattern used by engine_temp_sensor and other fixed
demos:
- Every callback takes callback_mutex_ and early-returns if the
  publisher has been reset.
- Destructor cancels the timer first, then acquires the mutex, then
  resets the subscription, timer, and publisher in that order.

Locally verified test_scenario_discovery_hybrid runs green against
Jazzy after the fix.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): validate peer-provided component_id against entity ID rules

parse_app() extracts the app-to-component binding from peer-provided
URIs (is-located-on) and vendor fields (x-medkit.component_id). Run the
extracted candidate through is_valid_entity_id() so that malformed or
hostile peers cannot smuggle path traversal, percent-encoded junk, or
oversized IDs into the aggregator's entity cache or response-side path
construction. If the candidate fails validation, App::component_id is
left empty (matching the "no binding" state).

Adds a regression test covering percent-encoded path traversal in
is-located-on, unencoded spaces, slashes in the vendor fallback, and an
empty vendor value. Each case must leave component_id empty.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(aggregation): read app-to-component binding from SOVD is-located-on

parse_app() previously relied on x-medkit.componentId (camelCase), but
the gateway actually emits this field as x-medkit.component_id
(snake_case) via the XMedkit builder in handle_list_apps /
handle_get_app. Older parser would therefore drop the app-to-component
binding whenever aggregating from a gateway peer.

Switch to reading SOVD's standard is-located-on relationship
(ISO 17978-3, section 7.6) first, and only fall back to
x-medkit.component_id if the standard field is absent. This:

- Works with any SOVD-compliant peer, not just our own gateway
- Matches what handle_get_app already emits at the entity root and
  in _links.is-located-on
- Supports both absolute URLs and path-only references in the URI
- Keeps vendor fallback for backward compatibility with older peers

Also adds a dedicated test exercising the standard-only parse path
(no x-medkit extension) with both direct is-located-on and
_links.is-located-on variants, and updates the existing relationship
fields test to mirror what real gateways emit.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(plugin_manager): declare YAML array params from --params-file

declare_plugin_params_from_yaml previously only handled scalar parameter
types (string, bool, integer, double). YAML list values in plugin config
were silently dropped with a "Skipping param: unsupported type (array?)"
warning and the plugin's configure() never saw them.

Add support for string_array_value, bool_array_value, integer_array_value
and double_array_value so plugin configs can accept lists naturally:

    plugins.my_plugin.peer_urls:
      - "http://host-a:8081"
      - "http://host-b:8081"

parameter_to_json in gateway_node.cpp already handles all array types via
the corresponding rclcpp::Parameter::as_*_array() getters, so once the
param is declared it flows through to the plugin's JSON config unchanged.

Also split the exception handling in declare_plugin_params_from_yaml:
ParameterAlreadyDeclaredException stays silent (idempotent case), any
other std::exception now surfaces as a WARN instead of vanishing into
DEBUG. Previously a YAML typo throwing InvalidParameterTypeException
would give zero operator feedback.

Suppress race:eprosima::fastcdr::Cdr::serialize* and deserialize* in
tsan_suppressions.txt. Flaky TSan races during rclcpp service Client
creation originate in the FastCDR buffer accessed from two threads via
TopicPayloadPool::do_get_payload, tracked upstream at
https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/issues/6340. Narrowed to the exact
symbols on the reported TSan stack so our own FastCDR misuse would
still be reported.

Fix four tests in test_data_read.test.py that used plain poll_endpoint
without a condition, accepting any 200 response including empty items
lists. Under TSan's ~5x slowdown the gateway populates the app entity
before the topic-to-app linkage completes, so the endpoint returned
{items: []} and the assertGreater check failed. Switch to
poll_endpoint_until with a non-empty-items condition (matches the
existing pattern in test_list_function_data on line 458).

Test hygiene in test_plugin_config.cpp: RAII ScopedYamlFile cleans up
the temp file on scope exit so an aborted test (ASSERT_* failure) no
longer leaks /tmp files. Array test also covers empty-string list
elements to lock in the null/empty substitution. New prefix-scoping
test covers out-of-prefix filter and dotted-key flattening.

data.message:

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(lint): add bugprone and special-member-functions clang-tidy checks

Enable bugprone-dangling-handle, bugprone-exception-escape,
bugprone-use-after-move, and cppcoreguidelines-special-member-functions
in .clang-tidy config. These checks catch object lifecycle and thread
safety issues at compile time.

Fix all 8 special-member-functions warnings by adding explicit deleted
copy/move operators to classes with non-default destructors (GatewayNode,
FaultManagerNode, PluginManager, TriggerManager, UpdateManager) and
defaulted destructors to classes with explicit copy/move (FutureAndRequestId,
RouteDescriptions, ScriptManager).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(fault_manager): serialize concurrent subscription creation in SnapshotCapture

Add node_ops_mutex_ to serialize create_callback_group() and
create_generic_subscription() calls across concurrent capture threads.

TSAN found a data race: when multiple faults are reported simultaneously,
each spawns a capture thread that calls capture_topic_on_demand(), which
calls node_->create_generic_subscription(). rclcpp node internals
(rcutils_hash_map) are not thread-safe for concurrent entity creation,
causing concurrent read/write on the subscription tracking hash map.

This race can corrupt internal rclcpp state and cause SIGSEGV on distros
with different DDS timing (observed on Rolling CI).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
ci: temporarily enable ASAN/TSAN for integration tests

Include integration tests in sanitizer CI jobs to catch use-after-free
and data races in the full gateway + HTTP + subscription path. This is
a diagnostic change to investigate the Rolling SIGSEGV in test_data_read.

Changes:
- ASAN job: ctest filter from -LE 'linter|integration' to -LE 'linter'
- TSAN job: same filter change
- Both: timeout increased to 30min, integration test timeout 120s -> 360s

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: defense-in-depth shutdown hardening

Cancel old timer before recreation in engine_temp_sensor parameter callback.
Cancel discovery_retry_timer_ in RosbagCapture::stop() for consistency with
post_fault_timer_. Add destructor to LongCalibrationAction calling
prepare_shutdown(). Add defensive executor->cancel() in test TearDown.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(demo): fix shutdown race conditions in lidar_sensor

Move initial_check_timer self-cancel inside callback_mutex to prevent race
with destructor resetting the timer. Cancel old scan_timer before recreation
in parameter change callback.

The initial_check_timer callback previously called check_and_report_faults()
(which acquires/releases callback_mutex_) then accessed initial_check_timer_
without the mutex. The destructor could reset the timer between these two
operations, causing a null pointer dereference.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(plugins): add shutdown guards and destructors to prevent SIGSEGV on Humble

Add shutdown_requested_ atomic flag, explicit destructors calling shutdown(),
and early-bail guards in callbacks for ParameterBeaconPlugin, TopicBeaconPlugin,
GraphProviderPlugin, and SovdServiceInterface.

On Humble, timer/subscription callbacks can fire after cancel() returns because
cancel is non-blocking and does not drain the executor ready list. Without these
guards, callbacks dereference partially-destroyed plugin state during gateway
shutdown, causing intermittent SIGSEGV (-11).

Closes #359

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: extract_plugin_config list_parameters prefix with trailing dot returns nothing

ROS 2 list_parameters() uses "." as hierarchy separator. Passing
"plugins.my_plugin." (with trailing dot) matches nothing, so
extract_plugin_config always returned {} for the YAML params path.

Fix: use "plugins.<name>" (without trailing dot) for list_parameters.
The substr logic still uses the prefix with dot, which is correct.

Add test assertions confirming the trailing-dot behavior and verifying
the fix works end-to-end.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): namespace ENABLE_WERROR option as MEDKIT_ENABLE_WERROR

Avoid potential collision with other packages in colcon workspace
when passing cmake args via colcon build --cmake-args.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway,fault_manager): fix format specifier portability issues

Use PRId64 with static_cast<int64_t> for portable printf formatting
of parameter values and chrono durations. The underlying type of
declare_parameter<int> and chrono::milliseconds::rep varies across
platforms (long vs long long), so explicit casts ensure format
specifier agreement.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): mark vendored cpp-httplib include as SYSTEM

The vendored httplib.h header triggers strict warnings (switch-enum,
old-style-cast, format-nonliteral) which become errors with our
selective -Werror flags. Mark the vendored include directory as SYSTEM
so compiler warnings from httplib.h are suppressed. On Jazzy the
system package is used via pkg-config which already treats includes
as system headers.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): demote -Wuseless-cast from error to warning

Type aliases (time_t, int64_t, size_t) resolve to different underlying
types across distros. A static_cast needed for portability on Jazzy
(GCC 13) becomes useless on Humble (GCC 11) where the types match.
Keep the warning for visibility but don't fail the build.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): suppress all warnings on vendored and gtest code with -w

Selective -Werror=<flag> overrides blanket -Wno-error, so per-flag
suppression lists are fragile and break across GCC versions. Use -w
(suppress all warnings) on vendored dynmsg sources and gtest/gmock
targets instead - these are third-party code we don't modify.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(cmake): use selective -Werror for flags safe from external headers

Replace blanket ENABLE_WERROR=OFF with selective -Werror=<flag> for
warnings that only fire on our code: shadow, switch-enum, old-style-cast,
float-equal, cast-qual, undef, zero-as-null-pointer-constant, extra-semi,
overloaded-virtual, non-virtual-dtor, implicit-fallthrough, format,
duplicated-cond/branches, logical-op, useless-cast (GCC).

Flags that false-positive on external headers (STL, ROS 2, nlohmann,
gtest) remain as warnings only: conversion, sign-conversion,
double-promotion, null-dereference, cast-align.

The relax function now suppresses specific promoted flags on gtest/gmock
targets instead of blanket -Wno-error.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): restore -Wnull-dereference, default ENABLE_WERROR to OFF

Restore -Wnull-dereference which was removed due to GCC 13 false
positives on STL headers. With ENABLE_WERROR defaulting to OFF, all
warning flags remain active for visibility without breaking the build
on different GCC versions. ENABLE_WERROR can be toggled ON once
external includes are treated as system headers.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(cmake): remove -Wnull-dereference due to GCC 13 STL false positives

GCC 13 with optimization triggers false -Wnull-dereference warnings
on standard library headers (streambuf inlining), breaking CI builds.

-Woverloaded-virtual, -Wcast-align, -Wnull-dereference,
-Wimplicit-fallthrough, -Wformat=2, -Wuseless-cast (GCC),
-Wduplicated-cond, -Wduplicated-branches, -Wlogical-op (GCC).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): switch to MultiThreadedExecutor for thread-safe subscription creation

SingleThreadedExecutor does not synchronize Node::create_generic_subscription()
called from external threads (cpp-httplib handlers) with its internal wait set
iteration. This causes non-deterministic SIGSEGV on rolling where rclcpp
internals are less forgiving of concurrent node manipulation.

MultiThreadedExecutor properly synchronizes subscription lifecycle across
threads. All gateway callbacks are already protected by mutexes (EntityCache,
LogManager, TriggerManager, TriggerTopicSubscriber), so concurrent callback
execution is safe.

This is the definitive fix for the rolling SIGSEGV in test_data_read.
The previous sampling_mutex_ + MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup fix reduced
the race window but did not eliminate it.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(tests): apply timer callback mutex to all demo nodes on humble

Commit f00a1563 added callback_mutex_ synchronization to rpm_sensor as
an experiment but never followed up with the other demo nodes. On humble,
TimerBase::cancel() does not wait for in-flight callbacks; if the
destructor resets the publisher while a callback is running, the callback
dereferences a null SharedPtr causing SIGSEGV (exit -11).

Apply the same pattern to all 7 remaining demo nodes with timer+publisher:
- beacon_publisher, brake_actuator, brake_pressure_sensor,
  door_status_sensor, engine_temp_sensor, lidar_sensor, light_controller

Pattern: callback_mutex_ locked in every timer callback (with null-check
on publisher) and in the destructor after cancel() before resetting members.

lidar_sensor required extracting check_and_report_faults_unlocked() to
avoid deadlock when on_parameter_change (holding lock) calls fault check.

Fixes recurring humble SIGSEGV in test_entity_routing, test_data_read,
test_entity_model_runtime, and any test using demo nodes.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): deferred topic resolution for triggers created before publisher

When a data trigger was created before its topic was discoverable (late
publisher scenario), resolved_topic_name was empty and TriggerManager
skipped calling topic_subscriber_->subscribe(). The trigger appeared
"active" but had no backing subscription - no SSE events were ever
delivered.

Add deferred re-resolution:
- TriggerManager stores unresolved data triggers at creation time
- GatewayNode wires a ResolveTopicFn (cache lookup by entity_id +
  resource_path suffix matching)
- TriggerTopicSubscriber's 5s retry timer calls
  TriggerManager::retry_unresolved_triggers()
- Resolved triggers get their topic_name updated and subscribed

Adds 3 unit tests for deferred resolution safety.

Fixes test_triggers_late_publisher flaking on humble where DDS
discovery is slower than on jazzy/rolling.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): thread-safety in NativeTopicSampler::sample_topic

Two race conditions in sample_topic() called from httplib threads while
the executor spins on the main thread:

1. create_generic_subscription from httplib thread races with the
   executor iterating callback groups. Fix: dedicated
   MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup for sampling subscriptions isolates
   them from the default group. A sampling_mutex_ serializes subscription
   lifecycle so only one sampling subscription is active at a time.

2. Callback lambda captures &message_promise and &received by reference
   to stack-local variables. On timeout, the function returns and destroys
   the stack while the executor may still be dispatching the callback.
   Fix: heap-allocate shared state (SampleState) behind a shared_ptr so
   the callback keeps state alive regardless of the caller's lifetime.

Adds 3 thread-safety tests:
- SampleTopicTimeoutDoesNotCrash (20 rapid timeouts)
- ConcurrentSampleTopicDoesNotCrash (4 threads x 5 iterations)
- RapidTimeoutWithActivePublisher (30 boundary-condition iterations)

Manifested as non-deterministic gateway SIGSEGV (exit -11) during
test_data_read on rolling CI.

fallback path for humble/jazzy/rolling = consistent builds.

context instead). Plugins received empty config and fell back to defaults.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(gateway): synchronize with worker before notify in ResourceChangeNotifier::shutdown

Classical lost-wakeup race between shutdown() and worker_loop():

1. worker locks queue_mutex_
2. worker checks predicate (flag=false, queue empty) -> false
3. shutdown() CAS flag -> true (NOT holding queue_mutex_)
4. shutdown() notify_one() - worker NOT yet enqueued on CV
5. worker enters wait(lock): atomic unlock+enqueue+sleep
6. worker sleeps forever; main blocks in worker_thread_.join()

Even though shutdown_flag_ uses seq_cst atomics, the worker's predicate
check and entry into wait() are not atomic with respect to the flag
modification. The notify can arrive before the worker is enqueued.

Fix: briefly acquire queue_mutex_ between setting the flag and notifying.
This guarantees the worker is either still outside its critical section
(will observe the new flag on the next lock) or already enqueued on the
CV (notify_one will wake it).

Manifested as a TSan-specific hang in DoubleShutdownIsSafe (worker spawn
+ immediate shutdown hits the race window).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: synchronize demo node destructor with timer callback

Timer cancel() does not wait for an in-flight callback to finish on
Humble. If the callback is running when the destructor resets the
publisher, the callback dereferences a null SharedPtr -> SIGSEGV.

Add a mutex that the callback locks during execution. The destructor
acquires it after cancel() to wait for any in-flight callback before
resetting members. Callback also checks for null publisher defensively.

Applied to rpm_sensor as an experiment; other demo nodes will follow
if this resolves the recurring Humble SIGSEGV failures.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: reset publishers and service clients in demo node destructors

Timer callbacks reference publishers via this pointer. Without explicit
reset, publishers are destroyed by implicit member destruction before
the rclcpp::Node base destructor cleans up timer entities. If a timer
fires during this window, the callback dereferences a destroyed
publisher - use-after-free causing SIGSEGV on shutdown.

Add publisher_.reset() and client_.reset() to all 8 demo node
destructors that were missing them.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: resolve flaky test_resource_change_notifier and Humble SIGSEGV in demo nodes

Fix two flaky CI failures (#344):

1. test_resource_change_notifier: reorder declarations in all 16 tests
   so ResourceChangeNotifier is declared after shared state (promises,
   atomics). C++ destroys locals in reverse order, so the notifier's
   worker thread is now shut down before any captured variable is
   destroyed - preventing use-after-free when wait_for times out
   under CI load.

2. test_hybrid_suppression on Humble: fix demo node destructors to
   reset subscriptions and timers before implicit member destruction,
   and restructure main() to explicitly destroy the node before
   rclcpp::shutdown(). This reduces the SIGINT teardown race window
   that caused SIGSEGV (exit -11) on Humble.

Closes #344

data.message:
fix: filter ROS 2 internal nodes via whitelist and configurable parameter

Three-layer defense against internal nodes (_param_client_node etc.):

   (manifest/plugin) instead of is_runtime_source() blacklist. Any
   non-protected source is eligible for suppression.

2. fetch_entities() filters _ prefix apps from peer responses at source.

   parameter (default: true). Works in all discovery modes.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(gateway): use timed_mutex with timeout to prevent permanent thread pool exhaustion

spin_mutex_ blocked indefinitely when a node accepted parameter service
but never responded to list_parameters/get_parameters. One hung thread
held spin_mutex_ forever, causing all subsequent configurations requests
to queue on the mutex, exhausting httplib's 8-thread pool and making the
gateway permanently unresponsive.

Replace std::mutex with std::timed_mutex. All public methods use
try_acquire_spin_lock() helper with kSpinLockTimeout (3s). If the mutex
cannot be acquired in time, return TIMEOUT error instead of blocking.
shutdown() uses kShutdownTimeout (10s) with best-effort cleanup on
timeout.

Fixes #332

from ROS 2 graph on each call. This missed topic-source and synthetic
components that are only present in the cache (populated during
periodic discovery refresh).

already has the complete entity set including topic-source components.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(gateway): use single pre-created param_node with spin_mutex for CI stability

Per-target param_nodes caused DDS discovery delay on CI (fresh node needs
time to join graph). Revert to single param_node_ created in constructor
(like original code) for fast service discovery.

Add recursive spin_mutex_ to serialize ROS 2 IPC calls (wait_for_service,
list_parameters, get_parameters) on the shared param_node_. This prevents
executor conflicts while keeping all other improvements:
- Negative cache (instant return for nodes without parameter service)
- Self-query guard (direct access for gateway's own node)
- Cached SyncParametersClient per target node

Remove per-node mutexes and node pool (no longer needed with spin_mutex).
Replace parallel timing test with concurrent crash/hang test.

data.author: mfaferek93
data.message:
fix(gateway): replace pool with per-target cached param nodes, restore default timeout

Pool-based param nodes created fresh SyncParametersClient per call,
breaking DDS service discovery caching and causing test_17 regression
(test_scenario_discovery_manifest).

Replace pool with per-target-node entries: each target gets a dedicated
param_node + cached SyncParametersClient. Per-node mutex ensures no
concurrent spin. Service discovery is cached across calls to the same
target. shutdown() clears the map deterministically.

Restore default parameter_service_timeout_sec to 2.0s (was 0.5s) -
the lower value caused integration test failures. Users with micro-ROS
nodes can set 0.5s in their config.

for nodes whose parameter service is unavailable (skip for 60s instead of
blocking on every request). Add self-query guard so the gateway never
deadlocks querying its own parameter service via IPC - uses direct
node_->get_parameters() instead.

executor conflicts without a global mutex. Reduce default
parameter_service_timeout_sec from 2.0s to 0.5s.

Fixes #318

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: proper action goal and subscription cleanup on shutdown

Add OperationManager::shutdown() called from GatewayNode destructor
to clear subscriptions, tracked goals, and service clients while
executor can still process pending callbacks safely.

Fix test action server to abort unfinished goals on shutdown -
destroying rclcpp_action::ServerGoalHandle without calling
succeed/cancel/abort triggers "terminate called without an active
exception" (SIGABRT). This was the root cause of persistent
test_operation_handlers crashes across all distros.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: three-layer protection against unbounded snapshot growth

Fixes unbounded snapshot accumulation when faults cycle between
CONFIRMED and CLEARED states (issue #308). Root cause: diagnostic
bridge forwarded every PASSED event without filtering, causing rapid
fault status cycling and snapshot capture on each re-confirmation.

Three-layer defense:

1. FaultReporter PASSED debounce: should_forward_passed() in
   LocalFilter applies same threshold/window filtering as FAILED.
   Previously report_passed() bypassed all local filtering.

2. Snapshot storage limit: set_max_snapshots_per_fault() on both
   SQLite and InMemory storage (default 10, reject-new strategy).
   Keeps earliest snapshots which are most valuable for diagnostics.

3. Snapshot recapture cooldown: snapshots.recapture_cooldown_sec
   parameter (default 60s) skips capture if same fault_code was
   captured within the cooldown window. Evicted on fault clear
   including auto-cleared correlation symptoms.

Also updates diagnostic_bridge integration test to send enough OK
diagnostics to meet the PASSED filtering threshold.

Closes #308

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: address review - remove dead prune loop, add domain bounds check

- Remove dead capture_threads_ prune loop in FaultManagerNode: joinable()
  is always true for unjoined threads, so the loop never erased anything.
  Destructor handles all cleanup.
- Add post-loop bounds check in integration tests CMakeLists.txt to catch

  the macro's built-in check).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: destroy executor before nodes in test_operation_handlers teardown

Simpler teardown order: cancel executor, join spin thread, destroy
executor (releases callback group references), then destroy nodes.
The previous remove_node approach still had timing issues on Humble.
Destroying the executor first is cleaner - after cancel+join, the
executor has no active work and its destructor safely releases all
internal references.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat: centralized ROS_DOMAIN_ID allocation for test isolation

Add ROS2MedkitTestDomain.cmake macro to ros2_medkit_cmake for automatic
domain ID assignment. Each package gets a non-overlapping range (DDS
domain IDs are 0-232, limited by UDP port formula).

Previously 9 unit tests creating rclcpp::Node had no domain ID
(defaulting to 0), causing DDS cross-contamination between parallel
test runs. All hardcoded ROS_DOMAIN_ID assignments replaced with
medkit_set_test_domain() macro calls. The macro auto-increments and
errors if a package exceeds its allocated range.

Domain ranges:
  fault_manager 10-29, gateway 30-89, diagnostic_bridge 90-99,
  param_beacon 100-109, topic_beacon 110-119, graph_provider 120-129,
  linux_introspection 130-139, integration_tests 140-229

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: remove nodes from executor before destruction in test teardown

test_operation_handlers TearDown destroyed nodes while executor still
held references to them. On Rolling, this caused "terminate called
without an active exception" during callback group cleanup. Fix:
explicitly remove_node from executor before resetting node shared_ptrs.
Also move executor_.reset() after node destruction since executor
no longer holds node references.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: join capture threads in FaultManagerNode destructor

FaultManagerNode spawned detached threads for snapshot and rosbag
capture on fault confirmation. These threads held shared_ptrs to
SnapshotCapture/RosbagCapture which internally use a raw node_ pointer.
When the node was destroyed on SIGINT shutdown while capture was in
progress, the detached thread accessed the destroyed node - causing
SIGSEGV.

Replace detached threads with tracked threads joined in the destructor.
Also stop rosbag capture (which has active subscriptions and timers)
before joining threads.

This was caught by removing SIGSEGV from ALLOWED_EXIT_CODES in the
previous commit - the crash was previously masked.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: remove SIGSEGV from allowed exit codes in integration tests

SIGSEGV (-11) was in ALLOWED_EXIT_CODES as a workaround for Humble demo
node shutdown crashes. This masked real crashes in all processes
including the gateway. With the subscription and client cleanup fixes
in this PR, processes should shut down cleanly.

Remove SIGSEGV to catch real crashes instead of silently passing.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: clear action and service clients in OperationManager destructor

The compat GenericServiceClient shim (Humble) stores pending promises
in a map. When the client is destroyed with unfulfilled promises while
a future still references the shared state, std::promise destructor
triggers "terminate called without an active exception" (SIGABRT).

Clear both action_clients_ and generic_clients_ in the destructor
before implicit member destruction. This ensures the executor drops
its references to these clients, preventing handle_response() calls
on destroyed objects.

This was the remaining cause of test_operation_handlers SIGABRT on
Pixi Humble after the subscription cleanup fix.

data.author: Bartosz Burda

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: filter synthetic areas for root-namespace node names

Runtime discovery created false areas from root-namespace node topic
prefixes. For example, /fault_manager publishing /fault_manager/events
caused topic-based discovery to extract "fault_manager" as a namespace
and create a synthetic area for it. These nodes belong to area "root".

Fix: after collecting topic namespaces, remove entries that match names
of nodes in the root namespace ("/"). This prevents per-node synthetic
areas while preserving legitimate topic-only namespace areas.

Added test: DiscoverAreas_DoesNotCreateAreaForRootNamespaceNodeName

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: prevent subscription teardown crashes and fix flaky tests

Add explicit destructors to classes that hold ROS 2 subscriptions with
callbacks capturing `this`. Without cleanup, destroying these objects
while subscriptions are active causes "terminate called without an
active exception" (SIGABRT) during test fixture teardown.

Classes fixed:
- OperationManager: clear status_subscriptions_ under lock
- LogManager: reset rosout_sub_
- TriggerFaultSubscriber: reset subscription_

Closes #315, closes #297, closes #296

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix: allow add_layer() after pipeline execute for plugin registration

The HybridDiscoveryStrategy constructor calls refresh() which executes
the merge pipeline. Plugin layers are registered later in gateway_node
initialization (after plugins are loaded and configured). The assertion
`!executed_` in add_layer() caused SIGABRT on startup for any gateway
using hybrid mode with plugins (all 3 selfpatch_demos).

Remove the executed_ guard entirely - add_layer() is safe to call at
any time since refresh() is single-threaded (ROS executor timer) and
the next refresh cycle will pick up the new layer.

Add regression test: AddLayerAfterExecuteDoesNotCrash verifies that
adding a layer after execute() works and the re-execution includes
the new layer's entities.

Fixes #307 (regression from initial fix)

data.message:
fix(triggers): fix ref_count mismatch, add bounded notifier queue

Remove the separate ref_count field from TriggerTopicSubscriber::SubscriptionEntry
and derive subscription lifetime from entity_ids.size() instead. This fixes a
mismatch where two triggers on the same entity+topic could leave ref_count=1 with
an empty entity_ids set after one unsubscribe, keeping the subscription alive but
silently dropping all messages.

Add a bounded queue to ResourceChangeNotifier (default 10 000 entries). When the
limit is exceeded, oldest entries are dropped and a single log message reports the
batch drop count, avoiding log flooding. Expose set_max_queue_size() for callers
that need a different limit.

Add QueueOverflow_DropsOldest test to verify only the newest 5 of 10 notifications
are delivered when the queue size is capped at 5.

code now switches on error code instead of searching for substrings.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(triggers): align resource_path format and fix multi-entity topic subscription

Data triggers never fire end-to-end because parse_resource_uri() captures
resource_path as a URI segment (e.g. "/temperature") while
TriggerTopicSubscriber emits the full ROS 2 topic name
(e.g. "/sensor/temperature") as resource_path in notifications. The
comparison in on_resource_change() never matches.

Fix by resolving the resource_path to a full ROS 2 topic name at trigger
creation time in trigger_handlers.cpp using the entity's cached topic
data. TriggerTopicSubscriber now uses the original resource_path (not
the topic name) in notifications, aligning both sides of the match.

Also fix multi-entity topic subscription: TriggerTopicSubscriber now
stores a set of entity_ids per topic instead of a single entity_id, and
emits one notification per entity. unsubscribe() removes individual
entities and only destroys the ROS 2 subscription when the set is empty.

data.message:
fix(triggers): address TriggerManager review issues

- Move store_.save() outside triggers_mutex_ in create() to avoid
  blocking dispatch during SQLite I/O. Persist before inserting into
  memory so failures leave no in-memory state.
- Clean up expired triggers from dispatch index and triggers_ map via
  new cleanup_expired_trigger() helper, preventing unbounded accumulation.
- Fix on_removed_ data race by copying callback under triggers_mutex_
  in remove() and guarding set_on_removed() with the same mutex.
- Replace sleep_for(100ms) with wait_for_event() + consume_pending_event()
  in tests that expect events; keep short sleeps only for negative tests
  (verifying no event fires) with explanatory comments.
- Reduce LifetimeExpiry test from 2s sleep to 1.1s.
- Reject non-positive lifetime in update() with validation error.
- Revert premature PLUGIN_API_VERSION bump (3->4); will bump in Task 11
  when PluginContext vtable actually changes.
- Add threading safety comments on TriggerState immutable fields.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(triggers): add TriggerManager with CRUD, condition eval, and hierarchy matching

TriggerManager is the central coordinator for the triggers feature. It
integrates ConditionRegistry, ResourceChangeNotifier, and TriggerStore
to provide full trigger lifecycle management:

- CRUD operations with capacity enforcement and condition validation
- Async condition evaluation on resource change events via dispatch index
- Entity hierarchy matching (components/areas scope down to apps)
- SSE synchronization (wait_for_event/consume_pending_event pattern)
- Lifetime expiry with lazy termination
- Persistent trigger loading on restart
- EventEnvelope generation with ISO 8601 timestamps

Also relaxes ResourceChangeNotifier filter matching: empty collection
now acts as a catch-all (matching all collections), consistent with the
existing empty entity_id and resource_path behavior.

29 unit tests covering CRUD, event evaluation, hierarchy matching,
SSE synchronization, lifetime expiry, and condition-specific behavior.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(scripts): fix deadlock in delete_execution, concurrency race, and atomic counters

Bug 1 - Deadlock: delete_execution held exec_mutex_ while joining the
monitor thread, which itself acquires exec_mutex_ to update status.
Fix: extract the ExecutionState from the map under the lock, release
the lock, then join threads outside the lock.

Bug 2 - Concurrency race: start_execution checked the concurrency
limit under exec_mutex_ but incremented active_execution_count_ ~150
lines later in a separate lock scope, allowing two concurrent calls to
both pass the check. Fix: increment (reserve slot) inside the check
lock scope and decrement on all error paths before final registration.

Bug 3 - Data race: id_counter_ and exec_id_counter_ were plain int
but incremented without synchronization from start_execution. Fix:
change to std::atomic<int>.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(locking): add LockManager core with data model and unit tests

Implement transport-agnostic LockManager for SOVD entity locking (issue #205, Task 1).

Core types: LockConfig, EntityLockConfig, LockInfo, LockError, LockAccessResult, ExpiredLockInfo.

LockManager operations:
- acquire: exclusive lock with optional scope restriction, break_lock support
- release: ownership-validated lock removal
- extend: ownership-validated expiration extension
- get_lock / get_lock_by_id: lookup by entity_id or lock_id
- check_access: two-phase access check with parent-chain propagation
  (App -> Component -> Area) and scope-aware filtering
- cleanup_expired: lazy expiration with expired lock reporting

Design:
- Primary storage: unordered_map<entity_id, LockInfo>
- Secondary index: unordered_map<lock_id, entity_id>
- Thread-safe via shared_mutex (shared for reads, unique for writes)
- EntityCache-backed parent chain lookups (no HTTP dependency)
- Configurable per-entity-type and per-entity-id lock behavior

37 unit tests covering all operations, error paths, parent propagation,
scoped access, config overrides, and disabled mode.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(test): replace executor.spin() with spin_some() loop in graph provider tests

executor.cancel() relies on DDS guard conditions to wake rmw_wait(),
which is unreliable on loaded CI runners (CycloneDDS). This caused
recurring timeouts on the Jenkins ROS2 Buildfarm where
spin_thread.join() deadlocked after cancel() failed to unblock
the executor.

Replace with spin_some(100ms) in a while loop with an atomic flag
so shutdown is deterministic and independent of guard conditions.
Add SpinGuard RAII helper to ensure the spin thread is always joined
on all exit paths (including early returns from ASSERT_* macros).

closes #284

- Increase clang-tidy CTest timeout from 1500s to 3000s (50min) and
  jazzy-lint job timeout from 60 to 75 minutes. The gateway codebase
  has grown and clang-tidy now exceeds 25 minutes on CI runners.

- Fix intermittent deadlock in graph provider plugin tests. The
  IntrospectDoesNotQueryFaultManagerServiceOnGatewayThread and
  HttpGraphRequestDoesNotQueryFaultManagerService tests added
  gateway_node to a SingleThreadedExecutor, causing GatewayNode's
  wall timers (refresh_cache, cleanup) to fire on the executor

  need to spin since DDS service discovery (is_available) works
  without an executor.

docs(plugins): fix introspect() example to match actual C++ types

The IntrospectionProvider code example used incorrect types:
- Return type was NewEntities but the interface returns IntrospectionResult
- input.apps was iterated as a map but it is a vector
- EntityInfo does not exist; the field is App

Replace with a correct example using IntrospectionResult, vector iteration,
and the metadata map (key = entity_id).

Also update the surrounding description to say "entity vectors" instead of
"entity maps", document both IntrospectionResult fields (new_entities and
metadata), and mention NewEntities.functions support.

Mention ros2_medkit_param_beacon alongside ros2_medkit_topic_beacon as the
second reference implementation (pull-based discovery).

Update the Multiple Plugins section to describe how IntrospectionResult
values are merged (new_entities vectors concatenated, metadata maps merged)
and note both beacon plugins can be active simultaneously.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): auto-register plugin routes in handle_root endpoint listing

Plugins can now describe their HTTP routes via get_route_descriptions(),
which handle_root uses to dynamically include plugin endpoints in the
GET /api/v1/ response. Also adds vendor_extensions capability flag.

- Add RouteDescription struct and get_route_descriptions() virtual method
  to GatewayPlugin base class (default returns empty)
- Implement in TopicBeaconPlugin (x-medkit-topic-beacon routes) and
  ParameterBeaconPlugin (x-medkit-param-beacon routes)
- Add PluginManager::get_all_route_descriptions() to collect from all
  active plugins (thread-safe with shared_mutex)
- handle_root appends plugin routes after static/conditional endpoints
  and reports vendor_extensions: true when plugins are loaded

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): implement stamp-based TTL for topic beacon hints

TopicBeaconPlugin now uses the MedkitDiscoveryHint.stamp field when
non-zero to compute the hint's age, back-projecting it into the
steady_clock domain for TTL calculation. When the stamp is zero
(default), behavior is unchanged (steady_clock::now()).

BeaconHintStore.update() now uses hint.received_at for last_seen when
the plugin provides it, enabling accurate TTL even for delayed or
batched messages. ParameterBeaconPlugin is unaffected (no stamp
concept - always uses steady_clock::now()).

Three new tests verify: received_at propagates to last_seen, default
received_at falls back to now(), and far-past received_at produces
immediate STALE status.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): add mutex to TokenBucket and unit tests for rate limiting

Guard TokenBucket::try_consume() with std::mutex for thread safety under
multi-threaded executors. Add reset() method to reinitialize rate without
move/copy (mutex is non-movable). Add default constructor, three
TokenBucket unit tests, and an integration-level rate limiting rejection
test that verifies excess messages are dropped.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
refactor(beacon): extract shared response builder and add entity validation

Extract duplicated JSON response construction (~17 lines) from both
TopicBeaconPlugin and ParameterBeaconPlugin into a shared
build_beacon_response() function in ros2_medkit_beacon_common.

Add entity validation via PluginContext::validate_entity_for_route()
before store lookup, distinguishing "entity not found" (SOVD 404)
from "no beacon data" (vendor-specific 404).

Replace hand-crafted JSON error responses with SOVD-compliant
PluginContext::send_error() using x-medkit-beacon-not-found code.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(beacon): security and validation hardening for beacon discovery plugins

- Add max_string_length (512) to ValidationLimits and truncate display_name,
  process_name, hostname, transport_type, and negotiated_format in validator
- Fix metadata key collision in build_metadata by writing freeform keys before
  structured fields so structured values always win
- Replace metadata merge-on-refresh with full replacement to prevent unbounded
  growth across hint refreshes (empty metadata preserves existing)
- Remove check_process_alive dead code from BeaconHintStore::Config, both
  plugin configure() methods, gateway_params.yaml, and docs
- Add config parameter clamping with WARN logging in both plugins: TTL >= 0.1,
  expiry >= 1.0, max_hints >= 1, max_messages_per_second >= 1.0, and param
  beacon poll_interval/budget/timeout >= 0.1
- Cap backoff_counts_ at 100 in ParameterBeaconPlugin to prevent overflow

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(integ_tests): add ROS_DOMAIN_ID isolation for integration tests

Each integration test now gets a unique ROS_DOMAIN_ID (starting at 100)
to prevent DDS cross-contamination between tests. Previously, stale DDS
participants from one test's nodes could leak into subsequent tests'
graph discovery, causing spurious failures.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(param_beacon): discover poll targets from ROS graph when not in hybrid mode

IntrospectionProvider plugins only get introspect() called in hybrid
discovery mode. When the gateway falls back to runtime_only (e.g., no
manifest_path), poll_targets_ was never populated and no nodes were
polled. Fall back to querying the ROS 2 graph directly via
get_node_names_and_namespaces() when introspection targets are empty.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): implement TopicBeaconPlugin

Subscribes to /ros2_medkit/discovery topic, validates and stores hints,
serves beacon metadata via REST vendor endpoint, provides enrichment
to merge pipeline via IntrospectionProvider::introspect().

Plugin lifecycle: configure() parses YAML config (topic, TTL, rate limit),
set_context() creates ROS 2 subscription and registers x-medkit-beacon
capability, register_routes() adds GET endpoints for apps/components,
introspect() returns snapshot mapped through BeaconEntityMapper.

Includes TokenBucket rate limiter, input validation via BeaconValidator,
and 7 unit tests covering message callback, introspection, validation
rejection, shutdown, metadata preservation, capabilities, and exports.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): scaffold ros2_medkit_topic_beacon MODULE plugin package

Creates the CMake/ROS 2 package structure for the topic-based beacon
discovery plugin. The MODULE .so target links beacon_common_lib via the
namespaced CMake target (ros2_medkit_beacon_common::beacon_common_lib)
and resolves gateway symbols from the host process at dlopen time.
Stub source and placeholder GTest are included; builds and passes tests.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): implement BeaconEntityMapper to convert hints into IntrospectionResult

Converts stored beacon hints into shadow entities for the merge pipeline.
Supports enriching existing apps/components, creating new entities when
allowed, reverse-mapping function membership, and building prefixed
metadata with process diagnostics, transport info, and staleness status.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): implement BeaconHintStore with TTL transitions and thread safety

Thread-safe store backed by shared_mutex providing reader-writer locking.
Supports insert/refresh with capacity limits, compute_status() for ACTIVE/STALE/EXPIRED
transitions, atomic evict_and_snapshot(), and per-hint get(). Config validates that
beacon_expiry_sec > beacon_ttl_sec and auto-corrects to 10x if invalid.
Avoids static thread_local to stay compatible with MODULE .so targets.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(beacon): implement BeaconValidator input validation gate

Adds BeaconValidator - the DDS trust boundary input validation gate for
all beacon hints entering the store. Rejects entirely on bad entity_id
(empty, invalid charset, oversized, null bytes); sanitizes function_ids,
depends_on, stable_id, component_id, and metadata in-place.

10 GTest cases covering all validation paths.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(discovery): make manifest and runtime layers independently toggleable in hybrid mode

Add discovery.manifest.enabled and discovery.runtime.enabled parameters
so operators can run e.g. manifest+plugin without runtime, or runtime+plugin
without manifest. Defaults remain true to preserve existing hybrid behavior.

RuntimeLinker is skipped when runtime is disabled. A WARN is emitted when
both layers are disabled (plugin-only mode).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
feat(discovery): extend NewEntities to carry Function entities through plugin layer

Add std::vector<Function> functions to NewEntities so introspection providers
can introduce new Function entities via IntrospectionResult. Update
PluginLayer::discover() to move and validate plugin-sourced functions into
LayerOutput, enabling the merge pipeline to include them in its output.

Add REQ_DISCO_010 to discovery.rst to cover this capability. Add two
TDD-driven tests: PluginLayerMapsFunctionsThroughPipeline (new functions
pass through) and PluginFunctionEnrichesExistingFunction (merge semantics
apply correctly when a plugin-sourced function overlaps a manifest function).

cache lookups always missed for root-namespace nodes.

data.message:
fix(discovery): address PR review - per-FG owner tracking, synthetic components, docs

Fix per-field-group owner tracking in MergePipeline::merge_entities().
Previously, all field groups used the first layer as comparison target
for subsequent merges. Now each field group tracks its current owning
layer independently, preventing lower-priority layers from incorrectly
overriding authoritative values won by middle layers (e.g., Plugin

so that setting it to false produces per-node components (legacy mode)
instead of unconditionally grouping by namespace.

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(fault-manager): isolate GTest unit tests from launch_testing subprocesses via ROS_DOMAIN_ID

The FaultManagerNode unit tests (test_fault_manager, test_sqlite_storage,
test_snapshot_capture, test_rosbag_capture) create in-process ROS 2 nodes on
the default DDS domain. The launch_testing integration tests (test_integration,
test_rosbag_integration) run concurrently and launch their own fault_manager_node
subprocess on the same domain, causing service calls to occasionally route to
the wrong server and making tests non-deterministically fail.

(62-65), keeping them isolated from integration test subprocesses that use the
default domain (0).

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
Fix Rolling build: use plain target_link_libraries when no visibility specified

On Rolling, ament_add_gtest_executable uses the plain signature for
target_link_libraries. Our medkit_target_dependencies macro was
unconditionally using the keyword signature (PUBLIC), causing CMake to
error with "all uses must be either all-keyword or all-plain".

Now the macro uses the plain signature when no visibility keyword is
passed, and only uses keyword form when explicitly requested (e.g.
medkit_target_dependencies(target PUBLIC dep1 dep2)).

test(gateway): add unit tests for AuthHandlers

Adds 15 unit tests covering the three AuthHandlers methods:
- handle_auth_authorize, handle_auth_token, handle_auth_revoke all return
  404 when authentication is disabled (default state)
- handle_auth_authorize input validation: wrong grant_type, missing/empty
  client_id, missing client_secret each return 400
- handle_auth_token input validation: wrong grant_type, missing/empty
  refresh_token each return 400
- handle_auth_revoke input validation: invalid JSON, missing token field,
  non-string token each return 400
- Error responses for auth endpoints follow OAuth2 RFC 6749 format
  (error/error_description) while the auth-disabled 404 uses SOVD format

Tests use a null GatewayNode and null AuthManager. Auth-enabled tests
exercise only input-validation paths that return before auth_manager
is accessed, so null auth_manager is safe.

Closes #178

Replace string-based backend error matching with typed UpdateBackendError enum

and all mock/test backends. Fix TOCTOU race in delete_update by creating Deleting

check before backend call in register handler. Remove dead Deleting phase check
in start_execute. Add stopped_ atomic flag to prevent new operations during
shutdown. Add execute failure/exception tests with dedicated mock backends. Fix

fix(gateway): fix global token waste, broken per-endpoint overrides, and TOCTOU in rate limiter

Reorder check() to run per-client before global bucket, preventing
exhausted clients from draining the global pool (DoS vector). Use
composite bucket key (client_ip|pattern) so per-endpoint overrides
apply correctly for existing clients. Compute X-RateLimit-Reset from
actual refill time instead of hardcoded 60s. Replace cleanup trigger
with CAS to prevent redundant concurrent cleanups. Increase test sleep
margins to reduce flakiness.

  responses without a CORS error

  to eliminate the data race on the cleanup timer field that is read
  without a mutex in check() and written under clients_mutex_
- Rewrite StaleClientsAreCleaned test to use 2 RPM so natural bucket
  refill cannot recover within the idle window, making cleanup the
  only possible path for the request to be allowed again

data.author: Bartosz Burda
data.message:
fix(reporter): break shared_ptr cycle causing SIGSEGV on Rolling shutdown

FaultReporter stored a shared_ptr<Node> back to the owning node, creating
a circular reference (Node -> reporter_ -> node_). This prevented clean
destruction and caused a segfault (exit code -11) during SIGINT shutdown
on ROS 2 Rolling, where rclcpp is stricter about cleanup ordering.

(create_client + load_parameters). The service client and logger are
self-contained after init, so no ongoing node reference is needed.

data.author: sewon.jeon
data.message:
fix: clean up pending_clusters_ when fault is cleared before min_count (#127)

When a fault was cleared before a pending cluster reached min_count,
the cluster retained a phantom reference to the cleared fault code.
This could cause incorrect cluster activation with stale fault data.

- Remove cleared fault from pending cluster's fault_codes list
- Reassign representative if cleared fault was the representative
- Remove pending cluster entirely if all faults are cleared
- Add 3 unit tests covering the fix

Closes #127

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

data.author: sewon.jeon
data.message:
perf: cache component topic map to avoid per-request graph rebuild (#184)

Previously, get_component_topics() called build_component_topic_map()
on every REST API request, rebuilding the entire ROS 2 graph each time.
This is wasteful since the refresh timer already calls
build_component_topic_map() every 10 seconds via refresh_cache().

Add a thread-safe cache (topic_map_cache_ + topic_map_mutex_) so that:
- build_component_topic_map() populates the cache after each rebuild
- get_component_topics() reads from cache instead of rebuilding
- First call before any refresh cycle triggers an initial build

This eliminates redundant graph queries on high-frequency API calls,
reducing CPU overhead on resource-constrained robot onboard computers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

data.author: sewon.jeon
data.message:
fix: reduce lock contention in ConfigurationManager

Release defaults_mutex_ before blocking I/O operations
(wait_for_service, list_parameters, get_parameters, set_parameters)
in cache_default_values, reset_parameter, and reset_all_parameters.

Each method now copies needed data under lock, releases it, then
performs I/O without holding the mutex. This resolves the 3 TODO
comments about thread contention during blocking service calls.

Closes #185
